📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A Commerce Department lawyer warned Intel not to treat the US demand for a 10% stake as a negotiation. The warning appears in court documents reported by WIRED’s Noah Shachtman, from a shareholder lawsuit against Intel’s board and the Commerce Department.

The lawyer, David Shapiro, spoke to Intel’s chief financial officer in August 2025. Intel’s internal notes of the call record his words.

Do not make the “mistake of thinking that this is a negotiation,” Shapiro said, according to the notes. “The President is expecting to announce a deal on these terms on Friday.”.

Sources indicate that intel’s directors received a summary of his remarks. In it, Shapiro accepts that the board could turn the offer down.

He also “noted that rejection will have consequences that [Shapiro] cannot predict,” the summary states.

Under the deal, the government released $8.9 billion in grants that Intel had already won. Most came from the CHIPS Act. In return, the government took about 10% of Intel’s stock for free, WIRED reported. Shapiro told the organization to weigh the value of having the administration on its side, including with customers.

The board’s minutes record doubts about the offer.

“The economic terms that had been proposed [by] the Administration were not, in their current form, attractive to the organization,” the minutes say.

According to recent reports, the directors approved the deal two days later. That day, Trump posted on Truth Social that the US had paid nothing for the shares. He valued them at about $11 billion.

Industry observers note that the pressure began earlier that month. Trump called on Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan to resign over his ties to China. Tan then met Trump in the Oval Office on 11 August 2025.

Intel shareholder Richard Paisner alleges that the board “caved to the government’s extortion.” Intel’s lawyers reject that account. In a motion to dismiss, they argue the board did negotiate. They say it won better terms, including the immediate release of the grants, WIRED reported.

According to recent reports, intel declined to comment to WIRED. The White House and the Commerce Department did not respond to the outlet.

The case sits in the US District Court for the District of Delaware. Judge Richard G. Andrews unsealed the complaint in June. He wrote that it involves what is likely a matter of great public interest. He has set a hearing on motions to dismiss for 10 December. Intel’s board and the Commerce Department both filed one.

The documents surfaced days after Trump mentioned he had “convinced” Nvidia’s board to bring Jensen Huang back. Paisner is also seeking Nvidia’s internal records on a deal that gives the government a cut of its China chip sales.

Tan, meanwhile, wants outside customers for Intel’s factories. Last week he said Intel had signed its first 18A customer.

In a recent development, grupo Financiero Galicia (GGAL +3.90%) reported third-quarter results marked by a sequential compression in margins as the Argentine economy transitions toward lower inflation and reduced nominal interest rates. Management reported that while headline profitability fell 16% from the second quarter, underlying operational metrics improved through reduced loan loss provisions and lower administrative expenses. The company stated that the integration of HSBC Argentina is contributing to significant efficiency gains, with group expenses falling 36% year over year. The group maintained high liquidity and a strong capital position, which management stated provides strategic optionality to accelerate growth as credit demand recovers.

According to recent reports, operator: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Welcome to Grupo Financiero Galicia Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. This conference is being recorded, and the replay will be available at the company's website at gfgsa.com. [Operator Instructions] Some of the statements made during this conference call will be forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the U.S. federal securities laws and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed. Investors should be aware of events related to the macroeconomic scenario, the financial industry and other factors could cause results to differ materially from those expressed in the respective forward-looking statements. Now I will turn the conference over to Mr.

Pablo Eduardo Firvida, Head of Investor Relations. You may begin your conference.

Pablo Eduardo Firvida: Thank you. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining Grupo Galicia's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. I'm here with Gonzalo Fernández Covaro, our Chief Financial Officer. The third quarter was marked by lower inflation and lower interest rates. Therefore, returns on inflation-linked assets declined and the credit cycle revealed signs of improvement. For Grupo Galicia, this produced a quarter with lower sequential profitability, but also with encouraging developments beneath the headline result. Credit indicators improved, provisions declined, expenses continue to fall, and our liquidity and capital position remained very strong. In our presentation today, we will first describe the operating environment and then the results of the group and its subsidiaries.

According to recent reports, unless otherwise indicated, all figures are stated in constant Argentine pesos as of September 30, 2026. The macroeconomic environment continued to combine fiscal discipline with softer economic activity. According to the Monthly Indicator of Economic Activity, MIEA, (sic) [ Monthly Estimator of Economic Activity, EMAE, ] the Argentine economy contracted 1.2% year-over-year in September, while edging up 1.1% month-over-month on a seasonally adjusted basis. Activity levels stood 2.4% below those recorded in December 2025. As of September 2026, the primary fiscal surplus reached 1.2% of GDP with total revenues declining 4.3% year-over-year in real terms and primary spending falling 2.3%. At the same time, inflation continued to moderate.

Consumer prices increased 5.8% during the quarter compared with 6.8% in the second quarter. This was positive for purchasing power, planning and the long-term development of financial intermediation. In the short term, however, it also accelerated the decline in nominal interest rates and reduced the returns generated by CPI-linked assets. During the last 12 months, inflation reached 33.4% in September. The monetary base increased 0.9% in real terms during the third quarter and declined 16.4% in real terms compared with September 2025. The average exchange rate of the quarter was ARS 1,500 per dollar. And at the end of the quarter, the exchange rate reached ARS 1,517 per dollar, representing a 7.6% year-over-year depreciation.

Dollar deposits remained dynamic, while in pesos, we see the transactional deposits declined year-over-year and time deposits gained share during the period. In terms of credit, the system data reflected the transition process of the macro. Real peso credit remained soft, while dollar lending continued to expand at a faster pace. In other words, the financial system moved toward a lower inflation environment, but the volume recovery was still uneven, with the volume of dollar intermediation becoming more relevant. Taken together, these trends frame our quarter. Lower inflation reduced the loss from the net monetary position, but asset yields declined faster than funding costs and volume growth is still lagging.

It has been revealed that as a result, margins compressed before loan demand and transactional activity had fully recovered. Against this backdrop, Grupo Galicia generated net income of ARS 229 billion in the third quarter with an annualized ROE of 9.3% and an ROA of 1.7%. The result was 16% below the previous quarter, but represented a significant recovery from the loss recorded 1 year earlier. More importantly, profitability remained diversified. Banco Galicia contributed with ARS 134.9 billion, Galicia Asset Management with ARS 48.5 billion, Naranja X with ARS 29.3 billion, Galicia Seguros with ARS 11.4 billion and Galicia Securities with ARS 5.3 billion. This diversification is strategically relevant as it helps to stabilize the group's earnings capacity.

For the first 9 months of 2026, net income reached ARS 577.5 billion with an 8% ROE. The performance indicates that the group has moved beyond the losses recorded in 2025 and is rebuilding profitability on a more sustainable operating base. The decline in profitability from the second quarter was largely explained by the reduction in the group's financial margin, which fell to 14.4% as lower lending rates, lower CPI returns and fewer gains from security sales affected revenues. But this should be read together with positive developments. The cost of risk kept on decreasing from the peak recorded in December last year and expenses declined materially year-over-year, improving the efficiency ratio more than 20 percentage points.

Industry observers note that banco Galicia, our largest subsidiary, is where the change in the earnings environment was most visible. Net income reached ARS 134.9 billion with a 7% ROE. The 19% sequential decline in profitability was primarily a consequence of margin compression, partially offset by the improvement in most of the lines related to expenses, in which our focus in efficiencies is showing results. During the quarter, average interest-earning assets increased 2% to ARS 32 trillion, but their average yield declined to 22.3% from 27.1%. Average interest-bearing liabilities increased 1%, while their cost fell to 9% from 10.1%.

Funding costs moved in the right direction, but not as rapidly as asset yields, which explains a significant part of the reduction in net interest income. Within the asset mix by currency, average peso loans grew 3%, foreign currency loans increased 9% and peso government securities declined 6%. This was a quarter of selective allocation with the bank reducing public sector exposure and prioritizing lending opportunities with an appropriate risk-adjusted return. Going to our interest-bearing liabilities, in the chart on the right, we can see the volume of those denominated in foreign currency, which increased by 6%. And on the left, that in pesos, they decreased 4%.

Interest income reached ARS 1.7 trillion, declining 12% sequentially and 24% year-over-year as lending rates and CPI returns fell. Interest expenses reached ARS 586 billion, also decreasing quarter-over-quarter. When we compare the figures with the ones of the third quarter of the previous year, the reduction was significant, mainly due to the increase in the cost of funding associated to the volatility of the midterm elections that took place last year. Fee income amounted to ARS 317 billion and decreased 3% in real terms in the third quarter, with most of the sources of fees behaving similarly, while results from financial instruments returned to more normalized levels after the strong gains recorded in the second quarter.

Sources indicate that FX results amounted to ARS 119 billion and increased 3% in the quarter, mainly due to the trading activity with our clients. The most encouraging development of the quarter was the change in credit trends. Loan loss provisions declined 12% sequentially to ARS 509 billion. The NPL ratio improved to 7.8% from 8.3%. Cost of risk fell to 8% from 9.3% and coverage increased to 96.1% from 92.8%. Fewer exposures migrated to Stage 3, deterioration in the retail portfolio slowed and nonaccrual financing declined. This suggests that the credit cycle began to stabilize during the quarter. We remain cautious as NPL levels are still above those recorded 1 year ago and improvement must be sustained over several quarters.

Recent findings suggest that nevertheless, the direction of the trend is now positive. The actions taken in underwriting, collections, portfolio management and provisioning are beginning to translate into better asset quality metrics. This is crucial for the earnings outlook. As the cost of risk normalizes, a larger portion of operating income can translate into bottom line profitability even in a lower rate environment. The second major structural message is efficiency. Banco Galicia's expenses declined 10% quarter-over-quarter and 36% year-over-year to ARS 731 billion. Personnel expenses fell 15% sequentially. Administrative expenses declined 5% and other operating expenses were 10% lower. These reductions reflect the efficiency initiatives implemented throughout the year and the benefits of the integration with HSBC Argentina.

Lower maintenance, IT, communications and administrative service costs demonstrate that the combined platform is beginning to operate with greater scale. The group's efficiency ratio was 39.4%. It increased sequentially because revenues compressed faster than expenses, but it improved by more than 20 percentage points compared with the third quarter of the previous year. Our objective is to continue simplifying the operating model while protecting customer experience, digital capabilities and the capacity to grow. Financing to the private sector totaled ARS 26 trillion and declined 3% sequentially, reflecting the softer level of demand and our selective approach to origination. Market share of financing to the private sector decreased 30 basis points to 14.7%.

Deposits were stable at ARS 28.7 trillion, while private sector deposits market share increased 20 basis points to 14.5%. Peso-denominated deposits decreased 3%, while dollar deposits increased 3%. Time deposits in pesos increased 12%, while transactional deposits in pesos decreased 11%, negatively affecting the cost of funding. Liquidity remained high. Liquid assets represented 99.7% of transactional deposits and 56.1% of total deposits. Capitalization was equally strong with a total capital ratio of 25.7% and Tier 1 ratio of 25.6%. Computable capital exceeded the regulatory minimum by ARS 4.8 trillion. This buffer provides strategic optionality. They allow us to absorb volatility, protect the franchise and accelerate growth when demand returns and risk-adjusted spreads become more attractive.

Recent findings suggest that the quarter also demonstrated the value of Grupo Galicia diversified ecosystem. While Banco Galicia managed the pressure from lower rates, the other companies contributed with other sources of earnings and customer engagement. Together, these businesses expand the relationship with our customers beyond traditional banking. They allow the group to participate in payments, consumer finance, insurance, savings and capital markets, creating a broader and more balanced platform for growth. Naranja X generated net income of ARS 29 billion. Its profitability declined sequentially to an ROE of 9.3%, but credit indicators improved. The NPL ratio fell to 17.8% and cost of risk to 17.9%.

The business continues to combine scale, digital engagement and financial inclusion while recalibrating growth to the current risk environment. Galicia Seguros reported net income of ARS 12 billion and a combined ratio of 92.8%, demonstrating the contribution of insurance to the group's fee and risk diversification strategy. Galicia Asset Management delivered net income of ARS 48 billion, while assets under management reached ARS 16.6 trillion. In a lower rate environment, the demand for savings and investment solution becomes increasingly important, and our asset management franchise is well positioned to capture that opportunity. Now Gonzalo Fernández Covaro, our CFO, will make some additional remarks.

Industry observers note that gonzalo Javier Fernández Covaro: Thank you, Pablo. Before taking your questions, I would like to add that the third quarter is part of a transition period. Lower inflation and lower rates are positive for Argentina and for the long-term development of financial intermediation, but they also changed the earnings equation faster than volumes could recover. This compressed margins and temporarily reduced profitability until volumes are recovered. At the same time, the underlying quality of our performance improved. Credit indicators began to turn, as we have remarked in calls -- in prior calls, provisions and cost of risk declined, expenses continue to fall and deposits remain stable and liquidity and capital stayed at very strong levels.

These developments gives us the confidence that the direction of the business is the correct one. We are moving from an environment in which earnings were heavily influenced by inflation, high nominal rates and financial assets towards one in which sustainable profitability will be driven increasingly by customer activity, transaction volumes, fees, disciplined credit growth and an efficient operating platform. Our priorities for the coming quarters are therefore clear. We will actively manage the balance sheet to protect margins and grow our earning assets. We will maintain discipline in origination and collections to consolidate improvement in asset quality.

According to recent reports, we will continue capturing integration and efficiency benefits, and we will deploy capital selectively as attractive opportunities may emerge across our subsidiaries, Banco Galicia, Naranja X, Galicia Seguros and Galicia Asset Management. So Grupo Galicia enters next year with a leading franchise, a diversified ecosystem and substantial financial strength. The quarter highlighted that even as earnings mix changes, the foundations of the business are becoming stronger. So with that, we are ready to answer the questions that you may have.

Talking about next year, we need to take into account that next year is a year with the presidential election that will may bring political uncertainty. So that's an improvement from the 8% on this year, ranging in the low double-digit range, I would say, for next year. We expect that, that will be like a step towards the 15% ROE that we are expecting for 2028. And by '29 and onwards, if with inflation accounting disappearing, if that happens, then our target is between 15% and 20%, closer -- more closer to 20%.

Gonzalo Javier Fernández Covaro: I mean activity is not that what we have seen is more demand for pesos, but for working capital short term, discount of checks, short-term lending, nothing really switched significantly for longer-term projects. Recent findings suggest that we need to see how the polls are, what the expectations on the -- if it's the current government or another government, which are the policies that they may implement. In a recent development, those reserves of the new portfolio are still a bit higher than the performance that those guys will have because, as you know, like IFRS 9 and how the reserve model works, you still need to use the experience of the last portfolios, even though you can do some adjustments to that. Industry observers note that tiago Pinho: Okay. Super clear. What about 2027? Can we expect maybe recomposed reserves by 110%, maybe even higher?

In a recent development, so what we are thinking is that we will analyze if we want to leave some of the dividends at group level to face latest opportunities of low prices for share buybacks. Today, we have that constraint that the holding company doesn't have much liquidity, and we cannot pay dividends at this point because of regulations. So we don't have a cash, I would say.

Pablo Eduardo Firvida: I would like to add one thing, Gonzalo. In the OCI, the bonds available-for-sale, most of them are in pesos, either adjusted by CPI or dual bonds and with very short-term maturity on average, I would say, 1.5 years, something like that.

In a recent development, gonzalo Javier Fernández Covaro: Yes, that's a good point, Pablo. On dollars, we have very small exposure. It's all peso bonds with very good yields, inflation plus 7%, 8% or TAMAR plus something high. So -- but, yes.

Gonzalo Javier Fernández Covaro: Yes. Regarding Asset Management, yes, it has been an notable part of our portfolio and our income. So we never see bank ROE by itself, even though here in the press release, we put it by itself. We look at it as the banking business ROE, then the fintech business, which is Naranja X and then the insurance business, which is what insurance tech giant, of course. But -- so for us, asset management is part of the banking business because it's the same customer, same everything.

Recent findings suggest that we -- yes, the new ETF, I think it's a good thing for the market, but we don't expect that to -- we expect asset management to continue with a very good performance and the customers to continue to invest in our funds. So we don't see any impact on the contrary. So we expect asset management to -- and the funds to continue to be an crucial part of our income. According to recent reports, so that's what we have been preparing for to have also other offers when the money market, the plain vanilla money market lose attractiveness, then what the other ones can bring. So we continue to expect to continue to keep and gain market share and continue to be one of the leading asset managers in the country and continue to have a good net income. And the other question talking about SMEs, small and medium enterprises, NPLs. I mean, it's true that NPLs for SMEs started after the consumer NPLs. For us, it's a small portfolio. So even though we saw an increase in NPLs, you don't see that in the numbers because it's -- the impact is not massive.

Sources indicate that we are starting to see some kind of stabilization, not reduction so far, stabilization. And by next year, we expect that those NPLs started to improve. But in the numbers of the bank, they are no material, so they don't move the needle in terms of NPLs as a whole.

SpaceX Sued by 2 States Over Grok’s Sexualized Images of Women and Children

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (746 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Oregon and Virginia on Monday filed lawsuits against SpaceX, alleging that Elon Musk’s manufacturer violated consumer protection laws, months after people used Grok Imagine to generate millions of sexualized images of women and children.
  • Sources indicate that grok Imagine is an image- and video-generation tool developed by SpaceXSI, a division of SpaceX.
  • In the lawsuits, separate but jointly filed, Virginia and Oregon allege that the sexualized images — including child sexual abuse material — were generated without the knowledge and consent of the women and children shown in the images and videos.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Oregon and Virginia on Monday filed lawsuits against SpaceX, alleging that Elon Musk’s manufacturer violated consumer protection laws, months after people used Grok Imagine to generate millions of sexualized images of women and children.

Sources indicate that grok Imagine is an image- and video-generation tool developed by SpaceXSI, a division of SpaceX. Shortly after launching last summer, the tool added a “spicy mode,” which enabled people to generate images and videos showing partial nudity and adult-themed videos. Grok Imagine is integrated into Grok, which is Musk’s AI chatbot.

In the lawsuits, separate but jointly filed, Virginia and Oregon allege that the sexualized images — including child sexual abuse material — were generated without the knowledge and consent of the women and children shown in the images and videos.

Read more: After Rampant AI-Powered Abuse, Grok Doubles Down.

Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones said in a press release that SpaceX misled people into thinking that their images and data would be safe.

“When xAI [now renamed SpaceXSI] allowed Grok’s creators to sideline consent to turn a profit, they prioritized growth and engagement over safety, and they deceived the public about it,” Jones said. “Today’s filings are the first step towards holding this company accountable.”.

Donna Rice Hughes, CEO of child internet safety organization Enough Is Enough, praised Oregon and Virginia for taking action against SpaceX.

“It is abhorrent that women and children are preyed upon in this manner and even more repugnant that xAI’s Grok ‘spicy mode’ has not kept up with bad actors who abuse their terms of service,” Hughes told CNET, adding that Musk’s “team can find ways to prevent criminal misuse of Grok, and at the very least, disable Grok’s ‘spicy mode.'”.

Industry observers note that grok Imagine introduced on Aug. 5, 2025, and within months, it was used to generate millions of sexualized images, which were posted on the social media platform X, which is also owned by Musk’s SpaceX.

Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield alleged SpaceX “knowingly designed” Grok Imagine and promoted spicy mode’s lack of safeguards as a feature, not a bug.

“It’s no surprise that Grok and X became a haven for perpetrators using AI to create and share child sexual abuse material,” Rayfield mentioned in a statement. “The lack of needed safety measures was considered a feature, not a bug, which they promoted as ‘spicy mode.’”.

During a 9-day span starting in late December, Grok posted about 3 million sexualized images, according to an analysis from the Center for Countering Digital Hate.

In a statement posted Monday on X, SpaceX stated that people using Grok to generate sexualized images and videos violated the platform’s terms of service and worked “aggressively to circumvent our safeguards.” The company said it tightened protections after the misuse and continues to test and adjust them as needed. SpaceX also said it notifies law enforcement authorities “when someone tries to break our safeguards and generate this content.”.

Industry observers note that earlier this year, several minor Jane Does filed a proposed class action lawsuit against xAI after people used their photos to generate child sexual abuse material using Grok via spicy mode. That case is still ongoing.

In a recent development, in July, a victim’s family also filed suit after photographer Russell Bloodworth in Arkansas allegedly used spicy mode to generate explicit photos of children. xAI went on the offensive, suing Bloodworth and South Carolina man Terry Wayne Harwood, who is also accused of using Grok to generate child sexual abuse material. The organization seeks damages for expenses incurred in fighting lawsuits and for reputational harm.

In a recent development, spaceX and xAI have faced lawsuits for other things aside from illicit image generation. The companies were sued for allegedly sharing sensitive data and for allegedly causing users to be hospitalized for psychosis after harmful chat conversations on Grok.

Sources indicate that monday’s lawsuits against SpaceX are among nearly 400 cases brought against 129 AI companies in the US, according to the AI Lawsuit Tracker. Many Big Tech companies have been sued for allegedly harming the mental health of adults and children. In August, Meta agreed to pay $18 billion to settle a lawsuit brought by US states alleging the manufacturer intentionally designed Instagram and other platforms to be addictive to children.

Companies such as ByteDance — owner of TikTok — Snap, Google and others face more than 2,400 federal lawsuits alleging that their platforms harm the mental health of children.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An email sent to freelance photographers says Photoshop’s latest upgrade uses AI ‘in ways that may not be apparent.’.

An email sent to freelance photographers states Photoshop’s latest update uses AI ‘in ways that may not be apparent.’.

The New York Times is asking freelance photographers not to use the newest version of Adobe Photoshop because features in the 2027 upgrade use AI “in ways that may not be apparent to owners.” In an email seen by The Verge and posted on Threads, two of the Times’ photography leaders, Meaghan Looram and Josh Haner, write that the use of these features “can result in metadata identifying photographs as AI-generated.”.

It has been revealed that adobe has spent the past few years filling Photoshop and other apps in its creative suite with a trove of AI-powered tools. The November upgrade cited by the NYT’s email adds several new AI features, including Adobe’s new “AI Assisted Editor” view, which lets customers access all of Photoshop’s AI features from a single toolbar. It also adds an AI assistant for step-by-step editing instructions, prompt-based image transformation and editing, new AI upscaling options, and an AI-powered tool that recomposes images for different canvas sizes.

It’s not always clear which tools in Adobe’s apps are AI-powered, and even some older options like automated selection tools may now be considered part of the AI suite. This can lead to photos ending up with metadata indicating they were edited with AI, which is a blunt way of describing what happened in post-production. For a newsroom like the Times, where photo editing is kept to a minimum, the metadata risks losing readers’ trust. Last year, the Times stated that it does not “retouch or digitally manipulate” photos but may “make minimal adjustments to color to ensure we are accurately reproducing the image.”.

It has been revealed that in August, Adobe began rolling out support for C2PA metadata across its apps, which indicates whether an image is AI-generated or edited using AI features. The NYT is issuing its restriction to keep these tags from inadvertently appearing in its photos. “At this time, we are requiring that all contributing photographers avoid using Adobe Photoshop 2027 (release 28.0.0 and subsequent updates) when working on assignment for The Times,” the email reads. NYT spokesperson Graham James confirmed the requirement in a statement to The Verge, which reiterated the policy outlined in the email.

Recent findings suggest that it’s still not clear which specific Photoshop features the NYT is referring to. Adobe didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for more information.

Upgrade, November 24th: Added confirmation from the NYT.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Starting this week, Uber riders in select markets will be able to specify that they want their trip recorded on video.
  • After a series of rider safety investigations and sexual assault lawsuit settlements, Uber began looking for ways to boost passenger safety and confidence in the service.
  • According to Uber, the knowledge that a trip is being recorded gives both riders and drivers peace of mind.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Starting this week, Uber riders in select markets will be able to specify that they want their trip recorded on video. The feature, which is being introduced in Baltimore, Indianapolis, St. Louis, and Raleigh, North Carolina, adds a newly introduced Recorded Rides choice to the app alongside other familiar ride options like UberX and UberXL. Uber claims that the new feature gives “greater confidence that a recording will be there if something doesn’t go as planned.”.

After a series of rider safety investigations and sexual assault lawsuit settlements, Uber began looking for ways to boost passenger safety and confidence in the service. The ridesharing platform first tested in-app trip audio recording in late 2019, then piloted the Record My Ride feature in 2022, before finally rolling out the video recording function in earnest, first in San Francisco in 2023, then nationally across the US in 2024.

According to Uber, the knowledge that a trip is being recorded gives both riders and drivers peace of mind.

While drivers can opt out of using the feature in their settings, more than half of its active drivers in the US choose to record their trips in the Record My Ride feature.

Starting this week, Uber riders in those four cities will be able to request a recorded ride during the hailing process in the Uber app and, when possible, be automatically matched with a driver using the feature. Choosing a recorded ride doesn’t affect the fare.

Record My Ride has been available to Uber’s drivers, though not passengers, for a few years now. The feature uses the front-facing camera on the driver’s phone to capture trip audio and video.

Uber states the recordings are encrypted and stored on the driver’s device to protect the privacy of drivers and riders, and are automatically deleted after a period of time.

“Uber can only review recordings uploaded as part of a safety report or insurance claim,” a representative told CNET.

In a recent development, not selecting a Recorded Ride doesn’t guarantee that your trip won’t be recorded in some way. Many Uber drivers choose to install separate dash cams in their vehicles, often with multiple cameras recording into the cabin. Uber offers drivers the option to register their dash cam with the service, but this is separate from the pilot.

“Drivers can use a separate dash cam, provided they comply with local laws,” an Uber representative told CNET in an email, “but Recorded Rides specifically matches riders with drivers recording through Record My Ride.”.

Uber says it’s exploring additional ways to use recordings to keep its riders and drivers safe. It will soon begin proactively activating the Record My Ride feature on drivers’ devices during trips that may benefit from additional oversight, such as late-night or trips involving teenagers. Uber is also looking into automatically turning on video recordings “when trips are not proceeding as expected,” such as when a trip goes significantly off the projected course or if a crash is detected.

Uber indicates it’s also looking into testing the automatic activation of audio recording on riders’ phones during nighttime trips. Passengers would have to consent to this, which would require the app to use their phone’s microphone.

  • MAI said it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

During the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced several fresh models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the company. But new model releases are almost a dime a dozen these days, and accelerating fast — what really stood out was how Microsoft will let its customers access those models.

Also: Microsoft states its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.

MAI said it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights. It’s essentially a selective approach to open-weight AI: more so than proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, but not fully downloadable on Hugging Face like Mistral’s Le Chonk. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account reps to get started.

It has been revealed that “You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay entirely yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Company to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents,” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of MAI, mentioned during the keynote.

The approach should stand out to businesses looking for affordable AI that lets them retain control over their IP. Microsoft stated it would only use customers’ information to train its models if they agreed.

“No one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model,” Suleyman remarked during the keynote, a nod to an argument Palantir CEO Alex Karp has made repeatedly.

Industry observers note that the dominant, if simplified, narrative in AI has been that proprietary, expensive models boast peak capabilities but aren’t customizable, while open, cheaper models are customizable but less capable. Microsoft’s AI models don’t necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the firm has legacy sway with countless businesses. By offering a customizable AI option, it could strike a balance among major tech companies.

Western labs, including Thinking Machines and Mistral, are releasing more competitive open-weight models, but Anthropic and OpenAI still have the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Though Licensed Weights isn’t an open-weight family of models, it does diversify the open-versus-closed debate a bit and differentiate Microsoft’s offering from OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s. It’s also a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal to balance price and performance, if businesses find it impressive enough.

Also: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026.

“Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot, MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and against Opus 5.5 it’s an incredible 5% of that cost,” Suleyman remarked of the newly introduced coding model the company unveiled at Ignite.

It has been revealed that the organization also released its upcoming image editing model, MAI Image 2.7, on Tuesday, which now leads the category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft has positioned itself for organizations seeking a reliable blend of ROI tools, customization, security controls, and capability.

Terrestrial networks cannot reach every location. Oceans, remote regions, and disaster zones often remain without coverage. 5G non-terrestrial networks (NTN) address this gap by using satellites and high-altitude platforms. Introduced in 3GPP Release 17, NR-NTN keeps evolving through Releases 18, 19, and 20. Satellite links bring latest challenges. In a recent development, after reviewing our fair share of foldable phones, we’ve narrowed down our top three picks for the holidays and the perfect person on your list for each one. Who knows, you might end up caving in and treating yourself to a brand-fresh device? (You’ve been warned.).

For more mobile gift ideas, from budget-friendly smartphones to wearable devices, be sure to check out the video below.

In a recent development, the iPhone Duo is far from the first foldable phone, but as Apple’s debut into the market, it’s generated plenty of buzz. The Duo’s superpower is its ability to integrate hardware and software, creating a seamless experience across both displays.

According to recent reports, the compact, 5.4-inch cover screen is great for sending texts and emails and checking notifications. The more expansive 7.6-inch inner display is ideal for multitasking, watching movies and working. It feels like using a smaller version of an iPad Mini that you can just fold up and toss in your pocket or bag.

The Duo is a great gift for someone who’s remarked they want a foldable phone, but refused to get one of the long-standing Android options already on the market. At last, Apple has its own offering that lets you stick with iOS. It’s a handy pick for people who often work on their phones and don’t always want to lug around a laptop. It’s also good for anyone who watches a lot of movies and TV highlights on their mobile device. Plus, as a phone-tablet hybrid, it’s just fun to use.

The iPhone Duo isn’t perfect. It doesn’t support Face ID, but Apple did recently add an option to unlock the phone using the front camera. This isn’t as secure as Face ID, so you’ll still need to use Touch ID or a passcode for more sensitive functions like using Apple Pay or accessing passwords, and after around 45 minutes of inactivity.

It has been revealed that the Duo’s cameras also aren’t as advanced as what you’ll get with the iPhone 18 Pro models, which have larger main-camera sensors and more advanced optical zoom capabilities. There’s also no telephoto camera on the Duo. Still, most people will be happy with the Duo’s 48-megapixel wide and ultrawide rear cameras, as well as the 12-megapixel selfie camera on the cover screen. The FaceTime camera on the inner display is best suited for video calls rather than snapping quality photos.

In a recent development, multitasking on the Duo is seamless, but it’s not as flexible as it is on other foldable phones. You can only have two apps open side by side, and you can’t readjust them.

Perhaps the biggest downside is the price. The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 for 256GB of storage. That’s why it’s a good idea to keep an eye out for any deals that can help lower the price.

For the Android-lover in your life, there’s no better foldable pick than Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8. Like the iPhone Duo, this phone has a passport-size design. (Technically, Samsung beat Apple to the punch, but let’s refrain from the “Who Did It First?” game for now.).

The Z Fold 8 has a 5.5-inch cover screen and a 7.6-inch inner display that’s great for watching videos, working and multitasking with up to three apps, which you can resize to your liking.

Sources indicate that it’s also very thin, measuring 9.7mm thick when folded and 4.5mm thick when unfolded. That means it feels similar in thickness to a standard nonfolding phone, even when it’s closed. The Z Fold 8 fits squarely in a palm and easily slides into a pocket – tiny women’s pockets included.

Industry observers note that like the iPhone Duo, the Z Fold 8 doesn’t have a telephoto camera. But the 50-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras on the back and the 10-megapixel selfie cameras do a solid job.

The Z Fold 8 is also priced on the higher end, starting at $1,900 for 256GB. But its compact, sleek design and versatility help to make up for that sticker shock. Again, it’s a good idea to look out for any deals, especially around the holidays.

Sources indicate that some people prefer flip phones for their nostalgic designs and compact size. Motorola has plenty to choose from, but the best and most affordable pick for most people is the baseline 2026 Razr.

According to recent reports, the phone features a classic clamshell design and a spacious 3.6-inch cover screen, making it easy to check notifications, reply to texts, control music or follow navigation without opening the phone. The 6.9-inch inner display feels like using an average nonfolding phone, even if the screen is a little narrower and taller.

For most people, the Razr’s 50-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras and 32-megapixel selfie camera on the inner display will do the trick. There’s no room for a telephoto camera, but the Razr pulls its weight for more casual photography.

The Razr’s processor isn’t as powerful as what you’ll get on the pricier Razr Plus and Razr Ultra, but as long as you’re not playing intensive games all day, you probably won’t notice the difference.

The Razr’s $800 starting price is significantly lower than the cost of book-style folding devices like the iPhone Duo and Galaxy Z Fold 8. The Razr could be a more appealing option for someone who doesn’t need a phone-tablet hybrid but just wants a phone that’s fun to use and taps into the nostalgia of the original Motorola Razr.

No matter which phone you choose, your lucky recipient will enjoy the holiday spirit long after the season has passed, all while making quite the statement.

This is probably the biggest addition to the next release of Ubuntu. And although you won’t find any major changes in GNOME, there are some crucial ones. First off, there will be editable quick settings, which allow for customizing, adding, removing, and rearranging toggles and widgets. GNOME 52 will also enjoy a revamped calendar popover, which streamlines the feature to focus primarily on events, time, and weather.

Recent findings suggest that desktop search is also getting a bit of polish by way of a redesigned popover and an improved results overlay that includes file previews, multiple actions, and search filters. And, as usual, there will be plenty of bug fixes and performance enhancements. The bump in speed is noticeable, too, in my testing.

  • In a report released this week, Counterpoint Research states the ongoing memory crunch led to a 24% year-over-year drop in smartphone shipments during Q3, “the second-lowest quarter since 2015.”.
  • It has been revealed that per the report, Samsung maintained its lead with a 35% shipment share, despite a 15% year-over-year decline in total shipments, well ahead of second-place Motorola, which captured 18% of shipments after a 23% drop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to a latest Counterpoint Research report, Apple increased its share of Latin America’s smartphone shipments in Q3 2026, recording the smallest decline among the region’s top five brands. Here are the details.

In a report released this week, Counterpoint Research states the ongoing memory crunch led to a 24% year-over-year drop in smartphone shipments during Q3, “the second-lowest quarter since 2015.”.

It has been revealed that per the report, Samsung maintained its lead with a 35% shipment share, despite a 15% year-over-year decline in total shipments, well ahead of second-place Motorola, which captured 18% of shipments after a 23% drop. Interestingly, Motorola’s share actually increased one percentage point from a year earlier.

Rounding out the top five were Xiaomi, with a 14% share and a whopping 34% decline, Apple, with a 9% share and a 10% decline, and Honor, with an 8% share and a 27% decline.

Despite the decline in overall shipments, Apple’s shipment share increased by 2 percentage points from 7% a year earlier, moving the firm from fifth to fourth place in the region.

Other brands collectively accounted for 16% of shipments, down from 19% a year earlier, with their combined shipments falling 37% year over year.

Here’s Counterpoint on Apple’s performance for Q3 in Latin America:.

Apple was the most resilient, with the smallest decline among the top five brands (shipments down 10% YoY), and rose one position to No. 4 in the region. Apple absorbed the impact of price increases better than its rivals, helped by strong product availability. Apple released the iPhone 18 Pro series at the end of the quarter. For the first time, Chile joined Brazil and Mexico in the first launch wave.

Sources indicate that as for regional factors that contributed to the decline, Senior Analyst Benjamin Corona noted that Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia faced additional challenges beyond the global memory shortage, ranging from political uncertainty to inflation and tighter household budgets. Smartphone shipments fell 22%, 26%, and 28% in those countries, respectively.

Looking ahead, Counterpoint indicates it “expects the decline to ease in Q4 2026 as prices stabilize and seasonal demand returns,” adding that “memory-related price pressure should moderate by Q2 2027, but supply constraints will likely continue through the end of 2027.”.

Breaking: 1Password Security Incident

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (693 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 1password

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, on November 19, 2026, 1Password began investigating indications that an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account.
  • Recent findings suggest that the attacker downloaded account records for a subset of our users.
  • Account and user identifiers, and account creation and last sign-in times.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, on November 19, 2026, 1Password began investigating indications that an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account. The actor used the account to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, which downloaded administrative data pertaining to our customers. This data included customer names and email addresses, in addition to non-secret internal metadata about the account. At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker.

Recent findings suggest that the attacker downloaded account records for a subset of our users. These records include:.

Account and user identifiers, and account creation and last sign-in times.

Public keys (which are public by design, this has no impact to user security).

Secure Remote Password protocol parameters (which cannot be used to access your account).

Tokens present in certain emailed links for invitations, provisioning and account recovery.

Other non-secret account metadata relative to our internal architecture (e.g. version numeric identifiers, file numeric identifiers).

The attacker also copied source code from private repositories and gained access to our CI/CD system. Our source code is not customer data, and contains no user secrets. CI/CD contains infrastructure related secrets in order for our product to work. We have triggered a rotation of all credentials which may have been exposed, and there is no impact to 1Password’s services, availability, or product security.

When we send an email to a customer to accept a provisioning invite to an account, or to accept recovery of their account, it contains a token. A provisioning invite is specifically used for our SCIM Bridge or Hosted Provisioning. During this incident there were a small number of users in this state, who have been specifically notified. This token is used to complete the invitation or recovery process, but only when combined with an SSO sign-in or a six digit code sent to the user's registered email address. The token is not able to get access to the account by itself. In order to reduce the ability for a malicious third party to successfully guess the code, we’ve expanded the code from six numeric digits to ten alphanumeric digits. This makes brute force guessing practically impossible.

Your vaults and the items in them.

The keys that protect your vaults.

1Password does not store your account password or secret key.

1Password apps and browser extensions.

Disabled the affected GitHub account, revoked the stolen token, and removed the access the attacker created.

Rotated or revoked all internal credentials which may have been exposed.

Lengthened the codes used in invitation and recovery emails from six digits to ten characters as a precautionary measure.

Tightened internal GitHub, CI/CD, and endpoint controls, and added newly introduced detections for this kind of attack.

Validated no internal evidence of user account takeovers or compromise using any exposed account provisioning tokens.

Brought in independent cybersecurity experts to validate our containment approaches and remediation efforts.

Be cautious about phishing attempts in the form of unexpected emails, texts or calls that mention 1Password, invitations, or account recovery attempts.

1Password will never contact you to ask for your account password or Secret Key. Only enter them in the official 1Password app, or on our official website, and only when you’ve opened the app or typed the address yourself. Your Secret Key is only needed the first time you sign in on a fresh device or browser.

Keep your Secret Key and account password safe.

If you see something suspicious, tell us at support@1password.com.

In a recent development, you trust us with some of the most sensitive information you have. 1Password is designed so that a breach of our systems can’t expose your vault contents. Your vault secrets are encrypted with keys that only you hold, so we can’t access them, and neither can an attacker who gets into our servers.

We are committed to transparency in the interests of our customers' security and the security of the broader industry, which is why we have published and maintained our Security Whitepaper since 2015. We’ll keep this blog post current, and we’ll update it if we find anything that changes what we’ve stated here.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nearly a year after showcasing their “luxurious” robotaxi at CES, Uber, Nuro and Lucid have started fully driverless testing on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area, the companies stated Tuesday.
  • The partnership, announced in July 2025, combines Uber’s ride-hailing platform, Nuro’s self-driving technology and Lucid’s electric vehicles.
  • Now, the partnership is ready to take its next major step, beginning with employee rides “soon,” the companies said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nearly a year after showcasing their “luxurious” robotaxi at CES, Uber, Nuro and Lucid have started fully driverless testing on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area, the companies stated Tuesday.

The partnership, announced in July 2025, combines Uber’s ride-hailing platform, Nuro’s self-driving technology and Lucid’s electric vehicles. Autonomous rides take place aboard the Lucid Gravity robotaxi, which I had the opportunity to see first at a CES showcase in January (in the form of a “production intent design”), and then on the road this summer, with a safety driver behind the wheel.

Now, the partnership is ready to take its next major step, beginning with employee rides “soon,” the companies said. They strategy to launch commercial robotaxi operations in the first quarter of 2027 in the San Francisco Bay Area, before expanding to Houston later next year. Lucid will begin manufacturing the first vehicles designed specifically for the commercial launch fleet “in the coming weeks.” Uber looks to deploy around 35,000 Lucid vehicles equipped with the Nuro Driver in the coming years in “dozens” of cities.

“Removing the safety operator from behind the wheel is an crucial milestone in our partnership with Nuro and Lucid, and a testament to all three partners’ focus on executing against our shared roadmap,” Samarth Kejriwal, Uber’s global head of autonomous mobility, said in a statement. “As we prepare for our first driverless passenger rides in the coming months, we’ll be working closely together to refine our operations, infrastructure and the in-cabin experience to ensure a safer, more comfortable ride.”.

Nuro indicates it’s been conducting “round-the-clock autonomous testing of the Lucid Gravity robotaxi on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area and Houston” since December 2025, with a safety driver in the vehicle who can take over if needed.

In May, Nuro received a California Public Utilities Commission Drivered Pilot Permit, giving the company the green light to conduct pilot testing for an autonomous passenger service with a safety driver. Nuro also received a California Department of Motor Vehicles Driverless Testing Permit in April, allowing it to test self-driving vehicles without a safety driver.

Uber’s partnership with Nuro and Lucid is just one of dozens it has with other AV companies, including Waymo, Zoox, Avride, Wayve and May Mobility. Adding driverless options to an app that’s likely already on someone’s phone could increase their chances of giving the experience a try — despite the trepidation many people have about self-driving vehicles.

It has been revealed that the Lucid Gravity robotaxi can seat up to six passengers, unlike rides from Waymo and Zoox that seat up to four. It has plenty of legroom and ample space for luggage in the back. The vehicle’s sensor suite is equipped with cameras, lidar sensors and radars for autonomous navigation.

It has been revealed that it’s been a major year for autonomous vehicles, and it appears 2027 will be no different. The rapid expansion of AVs comes amid heightened scrutiny. Last week, the California DMV banned Waymo’s robotaxis from state freeways after a series of high-profile incidents — after which Waymo paused all of its freeway rides. Waymo, the largest player in the AV space, has been involved in a number of other safety incidents as it expands to more cities. Over the years, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has introduced investigations into other AV companies, including Zoox and Tesla.

It’s against this landscape — and the full-speed-ahead race toward autonomy — that Nuro, Uber and Lucid will soon publicly debut their own robotaxi.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, some of the most popular Android smartwatches just got a battery-saving enhancement.
  • The v26.45 update concerns location tracking during outdoor workouts.
  • Watch 5: Is Google’s new model worth it?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, some of the most popular Android smartwatches just got a battery-saving enhancement. Google released an updated version of Google Play Services on Tuesday that can help extend the battery life of a Wear OS smartwatch.

The v26.45 update concerns location tracking during outdoor workouts. Wear OS smartwatch consumers can now use their phone’s Global Navigation Satellite System to track their location during an outdoor workout, which can conserve battery life by outsourcing the smartwatch’s energy to the smartphone when it isn’t in Battery Saver mode.

Also: Pixel Watch 4 vs. Watch 5: Is Google’s new model worth it?

Constantly communicating with satellites during an outdoor workout can be a battery drain, and every minute of battery life counts when you use your smartwatch for communication, workout tracking, and health monitoring. GPS services, a bright, always-on display, and continuous health sensors like SpO2 can squeeze the most juice out of your smartwatch.

Wear OS software is used by many of the most popular smartwatch brands, including Google, Samsung, and OnePlus. Both the Google Pixel Watch and Samsung Galaxy Watch’s largest batteries last approximately 40 hours. That’s nearly two days of use from two top Android smartwatches, but you’d be surprised how rapidly it can drain.

The show follows the story of Antonin Carême, who “rose from humble beginnings in Paris to the height of culinary stardom in Napoleon’s Europe.” Per Apple: “While he dreams only of becoming the most famous chef in the world, his talent and ambitions attract the attention of renowned and powerful politicians who use him as a spy for France.”.

Season 2 of Carême was revealed earlier this fall, and is expected to premiere in 2027.

I loved Carême’s first season and definitely recommend checking it out if you’re up for a French-language series.

Twenty percent of holiday shoppers are using AI agents as their first stop for research and advice, but they are not ready to have agents make purchases, according to the latest Salesforce research.

Also: What to know about early Black Friday sales.

Salesforce surveyed more than 2,500 shoppers in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia and found that 74% of shoppers trust recommendations from AI agents. Salesforce research forecasts AI-driven shopping recommendations to drive $75.8 billion in Cyber Week spending, up 13% from 2025.

Also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

Brands are also being noticed by AI agents, with 30% of shoppers saying they were first introduced to a new brand via AI. And most importantly, 1 in 10 (11%) shoppers would avoid a brand if an AI agent told them to.

Here are some of the key findings from the 2026 holiday shopping research.

Retailers that use AI shopping agents are seeing bigger orders and more loyal customers. The survey found that shoppers who use AI agent referrals are twice as likely to make a purchase. In addition, 39% of shoppers have used AI agents on an e-commerce site, and 80% had a positive experience, while 75% felt more loyal to the brand as a result of the AI agent experience.

According to recent reports, shoppers who use AI agents spend 8% more than the average buyer and purchase 23% more items per order. Brands that use AI agents are seeing seven times faster sales growth than brands without them.

Recent findings suggest that 1 in 3 consumers has used an AI agent, including the widely adopted Meta Muse, now used by 12% of all consumers. Grok Bot is also in high demand.

It has been revealed that the survey found that 28% of consumers give their agents multiple tasks per day. The most common use of AI agents is price comparisons, product reviews, and brainstorming for gift items. Brand discovery is a major benefit of AI agent use cases.

Recent findings suggest that agents as advisors are growing, but agents are not buying products yet, with only 19% of personal agent users using logic to check out. Only 9% of consumers allow their personal AI agents to have unrestricted access to their financial details, and 36% have set up a separate credit card for their AI agents.

Also: ZDNET’s favorite tech devices for 2026.

The majority of consumers (73%) are not comfortable giving personal AI agents their payment information, and 49% are not interested in agents making purchases on their behalf. Consumers do not want to share their purchase history or personal data that could potentially lead to unwanted charges. Shoppers will abandon an AI agent after 2-3 mistakes. If an AI agent makes a bad recommendation, 1 in 3 consumers will blame the AI.

Retailers must adopt AI shopping agents in order to compete. Retailers must be able to service and respond to shopper agents. The ability to detect intent, buying signals, sources of dissatisfaction, and other consumer-related buying patterns at machine scale (significantly faster and higher volume than human scale) will require retailers to invest in AI agentic engagement capabilities.

Also: 50 AI agents tried to build a thriving Minecraft civilization – it didn’t end well.

According to recent reports, today, AI agents advise consumers on their holiday shopping journeys, but in the very near future, they will autonomously make purchasing decisions with little to no involvement from their human counterparts. The future of shopping will be more autonomous, highly personalized, and nearly frictionless. Brands that invest in agentic AI will garner the most loyalty and future business.

By Keithen Drury – Nov 26, 2026 at 2:34AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

Nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) stock has gotten slammed over the past few weeks. It all started with co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang resigning from his position. While he's back in the CEO role, news of investigations into Nvidia's export controls are also weighing down the stock.

In a recent development, when the outlook is uncertain, that's normally the best time to buy stocks, as fear controls the market rather than logic. When you look at the growth Nvidia is expected to deliver, I think the stock is an absolute buy, and I wouldn’t be surprised to see it rise to $660 per share by 2028.

Sources indicate that that's a huge gain from today's levels, but how is that possible? Let's take a look.

There is no doubt that Huang built an incredible company, and he was an integral part of it. With him back in his role, the company he built remains intact. However, he's not the only one in the building. Nvidia has built a tech-centered company that has given it a huge advantage in the AI realm. Nvidia's products are better than the competition and practically sell themselves.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

Investors should keep an eye on the future, as product development is a major reason why Nvidia has created a huge lead. Huang returning to the CEO role is major news for Nvidia's product development. Huang has made several tough decisions over the years as to how to shift product development, and his vision and technical knowledge are unparalleled in the industry. Nvidia’s stock skyrocketed 31% on the day he was reinstated, underscoring this.

There will certainly be huge growth in the field, as several AI hyperscalers anticipate spending more in 2027, building on an already record-breaking 2026. AI demand is real, and Nvidia can produce enough computing units to meet demand. In fact, Nvidia estimates revenue will grow at a 75% pace in its next fiscal year. Some companies don't forecast that far into the future because visibility that far out is hard to achieve. But with the industry in a supply-constrained state, it's easier for Nvidia to estimate how many chips it will be able to sell.

Nvidia looks set to have another year of solid growth in 2028, although a 75% clip again likely won't be in the cards.

So, where will that put the stock price by then?

Thanks to the turmoil surrounding the leadership transition, Nvidia's stock now trades at a dirt cheap 16.6 times trailing earnings. I don't think that's a reasonable price for the stock to trade at, as I think a 30x valuation is far more reasonable, given its market position and growth prospects.

It has been revealed that wall Street analysts estimate Nvidia will generate around $424 billion in its next fiscal year. Assuming management’s 75% growth rate is accurate, that brings its total to $742 billion. Over the past 12 months, Nvidia's profit margin has eclipsed 60%, but I'll set it at 60% to bake in a bit of conservatism. That would mean Nvidia will generate around $445 billion in profits.

If we assume Nvidia can grow at an additional 20% year-over-year pace in 2028 (which is Nvidia’s fiscal 2029), that would bring its profit total to $534 billion. At a 30x earnings valuation, Nvidia’s market cap would be $16 trillion, or a $660 per-share stock price.

Recent findings suggest that that's a huge gain from today's levels, and it requires Nvidia to return to a reasonable valuation and meet projections. If it can do that, Nvidia's stock is a generational buy at today's price tag.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Introducing Intel One Mono, an expressive monospaced font family that’s built with clarity, legibility, and the needs of developers in mind.
  • It’s easier to read, and available for free, with an open-source font license.
  • Identifying the typographically underserved low-vision developer audience, Frere-Jones Type designed the Intel One Mono typeface in partnership with the Intel Brand Team and VMLY&R, for maximum legibility to address developers' fatigue and eyestrain and reduce coding errors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Introducing Intel One Mono, an expressive monospaced font family that’s built with clarity, legibility, and the needs of developers in mind.

It’s easier to read, and available for free, with an open-source font license.

Identifying the typographically underserved low-vision developer audience, Frere-Jones Type designed the Intel One Mono typeface in partnership with the Intel Brand Team and VMLY&R, for maximum legibility to address developers' fatigue and eyestrain and reduce coding errors. A panel of low-vision and legally blind developers provided feedback at each stage of design.

In a recent development, intel One Mono also covers a wide range of over 200 languages using the Latin script. The Intel One Mono fonts are provided in four weights — Light, Regular, Medium, and Bold — with matching italics, and we are happy to share both an official release of fonts ready to use as well as editable sources.

To install the fonts, please use the provided builds under Releases. Please refer to your software’s documentation for how to activate and use these fonts.

Sources indicate that we recommend using these fonts at 7 points and larger in print, 9 pixels and larger on screen. The .ttf, .woff and .woff2 fonts provided in the official release have been manually optimized for screen display, improving clarity and legibility, especially on Windows platforms.

Outside of the default characters, there are a few extra features that are accessible in some applications, as well as via CSS:.

Programming ligatures are not active by default. To use them, activate the stylistic sets of your preference in your code editor. For example:.

Recent findings suggest that you will find editable sources in the sources directory. The instances subfolder contains separate source files for each style of the typeface. Sources are provided in .ufo files, which contain complete artwork, links to OpenType features provided in separate .fea files, as well as meta information like naming and vertical alignments for each style of the typeface.

In a recent development, these are not installable fonts, but rather the source files that produce them: UFO (Unified Font Object) is an open, human-readable font source file format; you can find the file spec here. These sources were created using RoboFont. Many other font editors will also be able to open .ufo files; we recommend using RoboFont version 4.4.

In a recent development, for instances, you will find postscript and truetype subfolders; these contain separate source files for the .otf format and the .ttf/.woff/.woff2 files respectively. Since the format for the outline drawings differs between these sets of formats, for best results we recommend using the postscript sources to create .otf fonts, and the TrueType sources to create .ttf, .woff, or .woff2 fonts.

After making your desired edits, you can generate installable fonts directly from the font editor using its “Generate Font” functionality. If you use RoboFont, any install options should default to the ideal settings, but here they are for reference:.

It has been revealed that if you would like to apply edits across multiple weights, a more advanced yet potentially efficient way is to edit the masters. These are special sources that describe the extreme points in the design space — the lightest and heaviest weights for both roman and italic designs.

After editing masters, you will need to rerun interpolation to generate individual weights and styles within that design space. This requires the .designspace files enclosed with the masters. The designspace format is an open, XML-based format that describes interpolation spaces (format specification for reference). For a RoboFont-based workflow we recommend Skateboard for interpolation; you can also use the free DesignSpaceEditor extension to view and edit these files.

Note that masters are only available in postscript format, so they will be best for creating .otf fonts. If you need to make TrueType based builds from the masters, we recommend QuadraticConverter for best quality conversion of the curves before generating .ttf, .woff, or .woff2 files; mind that the results will not match the provided instances precisely.

NB: The prepared instances contain some additional data that cannot be maintained through interpolation. For best results, compare fresh interpolations to the existing instance sources and patch them accordingly, specifically the information accessible through the Font Info panels.

For TrueType-based formats (.ttf, .woff, .woff2 files), the official releases are manually optimized for screen rendering. These “hinting” sources are stored separately from the .ufo files, which do not contain any TrueType hinting information. When rebuilding TrueType-based formats, we recommend using the “autohint” option to achieve reasonable, though not identical screen rendering.

Sources indicate that if you would like to access and edit manual hinting instructions, you will find these in the separate set of source files under hinting/truetype hinting source. These special TTF files will be viewable and editable using Microsoft VTT.

If you have requests for edits or additions to the official releases, please open concerns and we will try to accomodate them.
