⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that although history conclusively shows that the stock market rises over the long term, getting from Point A to B on Wall Street is never a straight line.
  • Recent findings suggest that as of the closing bell on Nov.
  • It has been revealed that while there isn't a tool or metric on the planet that can ever predict, with guaranteed accuracy, when stock market downturns will begin, how long they'll last, and where the bottom will be, one time-tested valuation tool has a knack for forecasting substantial declines in Wall Street's major indexes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sean Williams – Nov 26, 2026 at 4:06AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

It has been revealed that although history conclusively shows that the stock market rises over the long term, getting from Point A to B on Wall Street is never a straight line. Over the past few weeks, the mature-stock-driven Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI +0.33%), benchmark S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.25%), and tech-inspired Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -0.62%) have reminded investors that stocks can indeed move lower.

Recent findings suggest that as of the closing bell on Nov. 20, the Dow and S&P 500 had fallen into correction territory, with respective declines of 11.4% and 11.6% from their all-time closing highs. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq is knocking on the door of a bear market, with an 18.1% drop since its Oct. 5 record close.

It has been revealed that while there isn't a tool or metric on the planet that can ever predict, with guaranteed accuracy, when stock market downturns will begin, how long they'll last, and where the bottom will be, one time-tested valuation tool has a knack for forecasting substantial declines in Wall Street's major indexes. This tool, with nearly 156 years of backtested history in its sails, offers a clear picture of how far the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite could plunge.

The S&P 500's Shiller Price-to-Earnings (P/E) Ratio, also known as the Cyclically Adjusted P/E Ratio (CAPE Ratio), is the valuation tool in question with an uncanny track record of accurately predicting the future.

Recent findings suggest that most investors rely on the traditional P/E ratio when swiftly evaluating stocks or the broader market. Though the P/E ratio works great for mature businesses, recessions that shift corporate profits into losses can make this traditional valuation tool useless.

By comparison, the Shiller P/E Ratio is based on average inflation-adjusted earnings over the trailing decade, meaning recessions won't adversely affect its readings.

Stock Market Shiller PE Ratio on the verge of taking out its Dot Com Bubble all-time high 🚨 🤯 👀 pic.twitter.com/CtCmSgWnLt.

In a recent development, when backtested to January 1871, the S&P 500's CAPE Ratio has averaged 17.45. On Nov. 20, it closed at more than double its long-term average (36.44). Over 156 years, the CAPE Ratio has exceeded 30 during a continuous bull market on six occasions, including the present, and the prior five were all eventually (keyword!) followed by declines in the Dow, S&P 500, and/or Nasdaq Composite ranging from 20% to 89%.

In other words, history shows that premium stock valuations aren't sustainable over the long run.

So, how far could the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq fall? While the Shiller P/E Ratio can't pinpoint a figure, the previous five downturns all retraced to a minimum multiple of 27, with several bottoming out at a CAPE Ratio of 20 to 22.

Industry observers note that the tricky thing with the Shiller P/E Ratio is that earnings growth makes this valuation tool dynamic. For instance, simple math would say that for the Shiller P/E to return to 27 from its Nov. 20 close of 36.44, it needs to fall by 26%. But given the ongoing growth in underlying earnings for S&P 500 companies, we're likely looking at closer to a 20%-25% additional decline in the S&P 500.

Given that the Dow Jones Industrial Average is often less volatile than the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite is typically far more volatile, history suggests the Dow would be expected to decline an additional 20%, with the Nasdaq likely staring down an additional drop of 30%, at minimum.

#132158. Zelda Producers: Ocarina of Time Remake Is a Bridge to the Future

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1031 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Zelda Producers: Ocarina of Time Remake Is a Bridge to the Future

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1031 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Over the last month, I fell in love with a upcoming game that’s actually old.
  • It has been revealed that I’m still thinking about (and playing) Ocarina of Time on the Switch 2, even with GTA 6 loaded up at home.
  • It has been revealed that I also can’t stop thinking about what a game like this means for Nintendo’s next wave of Switch 2 games, and a future Zelda game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over the last month, I fell in love with a upcoming game that’s actually old. It’s happened to me before, but Nintendo’s Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake drove that feeling home in a surprising way. How did Nintendo get me to fall so deeply in love again with a game I’ve already played? And why is it still winning me over, even with Grand Theft Auto 6 here?

It has been revealed that I’m still thinking about (and playing) Ocarina of Time on the Switch 2, even with GTA 6 loaded up at home. GTA’s universe overwhelms me, but it also makes me appreciate Ocarina’s focus and clarity. And it’s also another incredible graphics showcase for what the Switch 2 is capable of. Yes, GTA 6 is jaw-dropping. But so are Ocarina’s 60fps vistas and details. Zelda pioneered 3D gaming before GTA ever went 3D.

It has been revealed that I also can’t stop thinking about what a game like this means for Nintendo’s next wave of Switch 2 games, and a future Zelda game. Zelda’s previous games became increasingly open world, full of multiplying tasks and larger maps. It can get overwhelming. Ocarina of Time’s focus is smaller, but still tangled and immersive. Can the two concepts feed off each other? Will Ocarina help rethink where the next Zeldas are heading? And, maybe, where other open-world games are heading, too?

At Ocarina’s launch, I met in person with Nintendo’s producers for the remake, Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi, to discuss what it all meant and how the remake bridged the gap between the “old Zelda” and “latest Zelda.” Aonuma has been a producer for Zelda games since the original Ocarina of Time, and Fujibayashi directed both Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom.

For this project, they brought on staffers who’d worked on Tears of the Kingdom, many of them much younger developers.

According to recent reports, “In fact, some of them hadn’t even played the original Ocarina of Time on Nintendo 64,” indicates Aonuma. “We also saw this as a really interesting opportunity for this younger staff to make discoveries on the course of this project that they could bring forward on future Zelda projects that they might work on as well.”.

There are a lot more subtle visual clues, I found, even than what I remembered in Nintendo’s last two Zelda games.

“When we were working on Tears of the Kingdom, we had this very high capacity to express all kinds of details and this feeling of immersion in the world, and that’s something I think was a major influence on the remake,” states Aonuma. “Whether it’s a visual detail that you might spot from a distance that you may not have in the original, that could be something that draws the player in and suddenly gives them the motivation to explore.”.

In a recent development, what worked wonders, I found, was the quiet, subtle immersion, especially when exploring dungeons or figuring out solutions I’d forgotten decades ago. I had to study the environment for clues.

That’s the magic ingredient: a throughline in the Zelda games that Fujibayashi indicates is “the idea of exploration and discovery.”.

Fujibayashi appreciates how the visual tools have improved, even since Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom on the original Switch.

“A system that lets you share a high, dense volume of information visually provides new ways of giving clues to the player: They can use their sight to gather the information they need to do some of the puzzle solving,” he notes. “Even if you compare the graphics to Breath of the Wild, it looks slightly more realistic now. And that impacts how we approach puzzle solving and puzzle creation.”.

I think about Grand Theft Auto as the newly introduced benchmark for immersion and graphic detail, but I’m also finding that a lot of GTA’s discoveries are made through pop-up interaction graphics that let you know when something can be activated. Ocarina of Time doesn’t always do this. And I also can’t help but wonder: Could the Switch 2 achieve a way to run a new wave of impressive games using optimized graphics, even something on a level like Grand Theft Auto’s latest?

Or, rather, what if Nintendo aims for a newly introduced level of hyper-immersion in its games going forward, learning from Ocarina of Time?

According to recent reports, speaking of immersion, I kind of wish I could hold my Joy-Con up and use it like an ocarina in the new game. You can’t, although you can use the controllers to play notes or hum or play a tune into the built-in microphone using your own voice or instrument — something lots of people have been showing off online. But the Joy-Con-as-ocarina idea almost became a reality.

“To be honest, we did briefly think about doing exactly that, but then we also considered how difficult it is to turn the Joy-Con into something that’s going to make a sound that is faithful, and then also how to develop that into the application inside of the game as well,” indicates Aonuma. “What we ultimately decided to do instead was to have this audio recognition feature in the software where you can use any instrument that you would like, whether it’s analog or digital, and you can play these themes and have the effect in the game and experience that way.”.

Sources indicate that what I’m really hoping for is a Majora’s Mask remake, the second N64 Zelda game that built off Ocarina’s graphics engine. Nintendo could do the same here, although Nintendo wouldn’t answer my questions about Majora’s Mask during my interview.

I’m still unlocking all the little secrets in Ocarina of Time, sinking into the world as I go. And when I play the notes on my Switch, I imagine I’m playing that ocarina. After playing this Zelda game, I wonder what Nintendo could do with that same level of detail for Mario’s return on the Switch 2, almost 10 years after the last fresh 3D Mario game on the Switch. We might know the answer to that soon enough.

Tech Report: Pixel Weather’s new feature lets you report your local conditions now

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (412 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Default weather apps are notoriously unreliable, but Google is giving owners a chance to help improve things.
  • A recent revision to the Pixel Weather app introduced a fresh “Report current weather” card.
  • “Share the current weather condition,” the card states, “to improve local forecasts.” If you tap it, you’re given options to indicate whether the current temperature is accurate, warmer, or colder than the app says, and what your current conditions are, with options like cloudy, clear, rain showers, strong thunderstorms, and rain showers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Default weather apps are notoriously unreliable, but Google is giving owners a chance to help improve things.

A recent revision to the Pixel Weather app introduced a fresh “Report current weather” card. If the weather you’re experiencing doesn’t match what the app is saying, you can report the discrepancy.

“Share the current weather condition,” the card states, “to improve local forecasts.” If you tap it, you’re given options to indicate whether the current temperature is accurate, warmer, or colder than the app says, and what your current conditions are, with options like cloudy, clear, rain showers, strong thunderstorms, and rain showers.

In a recent development, the card also reveals what the app right now thinks is happening for you to use as the basis for your report. To find the card, scroll all the way to the bottom of your Pixel Weather app.

Also: Your best Google weather app alternatives (and what I recommend instead).

In a recent development, google said that it will use your feedback, device location, and “some diagnostic information” to help improve forecasts. Nothing you report will be associated with your Google account. The app doesn’t explain exactly how Google uses your reports, but I’ve reached out to see if the manufacturer can offer any details.

As someone who doesn’t put a ton of faith into default weather apps, I see this as a step in the right direction toward regaining some trust. Even if it’s not yet clear how Google will use the information you send, the goal of improving forecasts is an notable one.

Also: I switched to MyRadar as my main Android Auto weather app and don’t regret it.

A large part of what makes weather apps unreliable is that they lack human insight, and a computer usually can’t grasp the nuance of a local forecast the way a meteorologist would. Experts have also warned of reduced weather forecast accuracy due to recent NOAA budget cuts.

Industry observers note that the Apple Weather app has a similar feature, so it’s good to see Google catch up. I couldn’t find a feature like this for Samsung or any other native app. One of the most popular third-party apps, Weather Underground, does feature a “Report your local weather” prompt. It also gathers information from hundreds of thousands of connected home weather stations.

This new Pixel Weather feature was present on three Pixel phones in my home, so the rollout appears to be widespread.

Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1050 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
  • According to recent reports, high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
  • According to recent reports, the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

According to recent reports, high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

According to recent reports, the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

Industry observers note that spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

It has been revealed that the high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," stated Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he said.

Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

"The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone remarked.

He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

That said, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

Industry observers note that "There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, remarked Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

Sources indicate that "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she said.

Recent findings suggest that the lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, said Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

According to recent reports, the overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he remarked. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

In addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she said.

Industry observers note that "It is isolated," she remarked. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

"We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she noted.

Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

But there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

Recent findings suggest that "We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin stated. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

Recent findings suggest that it's also key to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, mentioned R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

"With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo said.

It has been revealed that "That's when spreads really widen out," he noted. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 10 stocks we like better than iShares Bitcoin Trust ›.
  • It is Form 13F filing season, meaning it's a good time to bone up on exactly what that regulatory document is.
  • Likely due in part to some investors' reverence for Warren Buffett, among other famous professional market participants, following 13F filings is something of a sport.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Todd Shriber – Nov 26, 2026 at 4:30AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than iShares Bitcoin Trust ›.

It is Form 13F filing season, meaning it's a good time to bone up on exactly what that regulatory document is. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) requires that investors exercising "investment discretion over $100 million or more" reveal their holdings in Form 13F within 45 days of the end of the prior quarter.

Likely due in part to some investors' reverence for Warren Buffett, among other famous professional market participants, following 13F filings is something of a sport. However, it's not always the best way to track what the smart money is doing.

Recent findings suggest that wells Fargo increased its holdings of the iShares Bitcoin Trust, but that’s not a buy signal. Image source: Getty Images.

Take the case of Wells Fargo (WFC -0.31%) and the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT +0.92%), the largest spot Bitcoin (BTC +4.19%) exchange-traded fund (ETF).

In a recent development, third-quarter 13F filings indicate that several banks, including Wells Fargo, increased exposure to various spot Bitcoin ETFs. On the surface, that may be all some investors need to know before grabbing for the falling knife (hopefully a temporary condition) that is the world's largest cryptocurrency.

Indeed, Wells Fargo more than doubled its holdings of the iShares Bitcoin Trust to nearly 49.6 million, worth about $2.4 billion, as of the end of the third quarter. Investors need to dig deeper than that. Here's why: roughly 85% of the bank's position in the king of Bitcoin ETFs is held on behalf of brokerage clients.

In a recent development, put another way, the bulk of Wells Fargo's stake in the Bitcoin ETF is attributable to folks who trade on the bank's platform or to clients of Wells Fargo Advisors – the bank's wealth management arm. That means that the bank, for the most part, is NOT directly making a directional bet on the iShares ETFs. It's merely taking custody of the fund on behalf of its customers who own it.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

Wells Fargo's involvement with the Bitcoin ETF isn't comparable to, say, Berkshire Hathaway revealing a newly introduced position or adding to an existing holding. News to that effect often boosts the stock in question because Berkshire is making a clear bullish bet. That's simply not the case with Wells Fargo and this Bitcoin ETF.

It has been revealed that bitcoin bulls  (sometimes known in crypto lingo as HODLers) who are disappointed by the revelation that Wells Fargo's big boost to its Bitcoin ETF position means little can take heart, as there are some encouraging signs in other 13Fs. For example, Wall Street firms added $4.2 billion in Bitcoin ETFs in the third quarter, and institutional holdings of those ETFs hit a record in the July-September period.

Importantly, some of those professional investors are using Bitcoin ETFs to make directional bets. Plus, data confirm that some well-known hedge fund managers either added to or initiated positions in the iShares ETF in the third quarter.

Still, caution is warranted because some recent buyers of Bitcoin ETFs may have already ditched those positions, and the investing public won't know that until fourth-quarter 13Fs come out next year.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that in an effort to cut costs after two quarters of consecutive losses and amid global RAM shortages, Samsung Electronics’ Mobile Business division will switch from an annual release schedule to a biannual one for its smartwatches, according to ET News.
  • I am not mad at this decision by Samsung.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You might have to wait over a year to get the Samsung Galaxy Watch 10: Samsung will not release any new Galaxy smartwatch in 2027, South Korea’s ET News reported on Sunday.

Industry observers note that in an effort to cut costs after two quarters of consecutive losses and amid global RAM shortages, Samsung Electronics’ Mobile Business division will switch from an annual release schedule to a biannual one for its smartwatches, according to ET News. The switch follows other cost-cutting measures that will reduce production of the tech giant’s midrange smartphone lineup while increasing its premium Galaxy S27 offerings.

I am not mad at this decision by Samsung. Annual smartwatch updates are usually iterative anyway. Take Apple, for example. Its Apple Watch Series 10, released in 2024, had the same chip as the Apple Watch Series 11, released a year later. The most recent Apple Watch, the Apple Watch Series 12, has the same battery life as the Apple Watch Series 11. I’d expect Apple to keep its new sensors, which debuted on the Series 12 and Ultra 4, for its Series 13 or Ultra 5 next year.

Samsung’s Galaxy Watch 9, which debuted with a different chip and added a few more hours of battery, had the same bones as the Galaxy Watch 8.

If some of the biggest features on these smartwatches remain the same for a few years, why not change the release schedule to a biannual one?

In a recent development, also: Galaxy Watch 9 vs. Galaxy Watch 8: I’ve compared both models, here’s my advice.

Some of the most substantial updates that arrive on new devices like the Galaxy Watch 9 or Apple Watch Series 12 normally arrive through software updates, which end up landing on previous watch generations upon launch as well.

By switching from an annual release cycle to a biannual one, Samsung could drum up more excitement and anticipation between releases, and be able to surprise its customers with more purchase-worthy updates.

Samsung did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that apple’s Mac lineup is stronger than ever this year, largely thanks to the fresh MacBook Neo.
  • In a recent development, the MacBook Neo is Apple’s most affordable laptop ever, starting at $699 (presently on sale for $599).
  • Sources indicate that unlike Apple’s other Macs, the MacBook Neo is powered by an A-series chip rather than an M-series chip.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that apple’s Mac lineup is stronger than ever this year, largely thanks to the fresh MacBook Neo. If you’re deciding between the MacBook Neo and the MacBook Air this holiday season, here’s everything you need to know.

In a recent development, the MacBook Neo is Apple’s most affordable laptop ever, starting at $699 (presently on sale for $599). It features a solid aluminum design that comes in a range of fun colors, including Silver, Blush, Citrus, and Indigo.

Sources indicate that unlike Apple’s other Macs, the MacBook Neo is powered by an A-series chip rather than an M-series chip. It uses the A18 Pro chip originally introduced with the iPhone 16 Pro, featuring a 6-core CPU and 5-core GPU.

The MacBook Neo comes with 8GB of unified memory, with no additional RAM configuration options available. It starts with 256GB of storage, with a 512GB configuration available for an additional $100. That $100 upgrade also gets you Touch ID, which is not included in the base model.

There are some other trade-offs compared to the MacBook Air. The MacBook Neo lacks a backlit keyboard, MagSafe charging, and a Force Touch trackpad. It also has more limited USB-C connectivity and supports just one external display.

Recent findings suggest that still, the MacBook Neo offers an impressive feature set. It has a 13-inch display, up to 16 hours of battery life, a 1080p FaceTime camera, and the full macOS experience.

Recent findings suggest that the MacBook Air, meanwhile, was updated earlier this year with Apple’s M5 chip. It starts at $1,299, making it $600 more expensive than the entry-level MacBook Air. The MacBook Air is presently on sale with a starting price of $999.

In a recent development, for that $600 upgrade, the MacBook Air offers several key advantages over the MacBook Air. The M5 chip has a 10-core CPU and up to a 10-core GPU, enabling better sustained performance than the MacBook Neo.

The MacBook Air also starts with 16GB of unified memory and 512GB of storage, both double the entry-level MacBook Neo. You can configure it with up to 32GB of memory and 4TB of storage, while the MacBook Neo is limited to 8GB of memory and 512GB of storage.

Apple rates the MacBook Air for up to 18 hours of video streaming and 15 hours of wireless web browsing, compared to 16 hours and 11 hours, respectively, for the MacBook Neo.

As I wrote in my review earlier this year, I think the MacBook Neo is a great Mac, full stop … not just because of the great price. It can handle the vast majority of things most people will throw at it. This includes web browsing, basic photo and video editing, research, and much more.

The M5 MacBook Air, meanwhile, offers more power and more configuration options. This makes it a great option for people who need more storage, RAM, and power than the MacBook Neo can offer.

It has been revealed that one of my favorite things about the MacBook Air is that it’s available in two screen sizes. The 15-inch MacBook Air is one of my favorite Apple laptops with a combination of the ultra-thin and light design and the larger screen. I think a lot of people forget it exists, but it’s an excellent choice.

It has been revealed that to recap, I think the MacBook Neo is a great choice for everyday tasks like web browsing, email, writing, and streaming. The MacBook Air is a better fit for more demanding workflows, including photo and video editing, coding, working with large spreadsheets, and heavy multitasking.

Beyond performance, the MacBook Air offers a handful of niceties that you won’t find on the MacBook Neo. These include a backlit keyboard, a larger display with True Tone, MagSafe charging, a better webcam and speakers, and a Force Touch trackpad. It also includes Touch ID on every configuration, longer battery life, and support for two external displays.

In a recent development, if it’s in the budget, I think the MacBook Air is an excellent choice for all Mac shoppers. It’s plenty powerful, thin and light, and is highly configurable compared to the MacBook Neo.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The music streaming app confirmed on Tuesday that it is banning all tracks it determines to be entirely AI-generated.
  • The app also stated distributors, such as DistroKid, TuneCore, CD Baby and others, would not be allowed to deliver wholly AI-generated music.
  • According to Tidal, 43% of tracks distributed to the app over the past three months were completely AI-generated, including 60% of the music submitted on Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The flood is too much for Tidal. The music streaming app confirmed on Tuesday that it is banning all tracks it determines to be entirely AI-generated. The platform mentioned it’s making the move after being increasingly inundated with non-human music. As of Dec. 9, Tidal will no longer accept or host fully AI-generated tracks.

The app also stated distributors, such as DistroKid, TuneCore, CD Baby and others, would not be allowed to deliver wholly AI-generated music.

According to Tidal, 43% of tracks distributed to the app over the past three months were completely AI-generated, including 60% of the music submitted on Nov. 6 alone. Tidal noted the affected tracks were labeled as AI and removed from the royalty pool, which is the pot of subscription and ad revenue paid out to rights holders.

Before Tuesday’s action, Tidal had tried to lessen AI’s influence by identifying, labeling and demonetizing AI tracks, as outlined in its AI policy. But amid the growing influx of AI music, representatives for the app stated it was time for “a more drastic change.”.

Tidal noted there are 27 million tracks in its catalog that are 100% AI, but 96% of them have not been streamed at all in the past three months. Those 27 million tracks make up 6.3% of Tidal’s entire listings.

The manufacturer has removed more than 65,000 tracks flagged for artist-name impersonation.

Some AI help is permitted. Musical tracks where the maker used AI assistance but did not rely on it to generate the entire track will be allowed on the platform. Tidal uses ⁠Ircam Amplify to detect AI.

A Tidal representative told CNET that the app does not set a maximum amount of AI assistance that can be used to make tracks, and affirmed that only tracks that are deemed 100% AI-generated would be removed.

Industry observers note that read more: I Only Listened to AI Music for a Week. It Was Terrible, but Not for the Reason You Think.

According to recent reports, “Tidal will always fight for artists to get paid more,” the company said in its announcement. “Everything in this update comes back to that. If you make music, you should be able to put it on Tidal knowing it won’t be buried under tracks no one asked for or copied by someone pretending to be you.”.

Industry observers note that generating music with AI is increasingly easy with online tools. The AI song-generation platform Suno can create songs using only text prompts. With Google’s Lyria, you can use photos or text prompts to generate tracks up to 3 minutes long.

Recent findings suggest that AI music also is not just about creating hit songs. Some industries need affordable music for short-form videos, games, apps and retail spaces, and they are increasingly turning to AI to supply it.

But streaming apps and other companies are fighting back against AI slop, which refers to often poor-quality AI-generated social media posts, articles, music, videos and images inundating the internet in an attempt to generate click-and-stream revenue.

YouTube recently rolled out a fresh labeling system to indicate which music is AI-generated. Deezer provides a free tool listeners can use to see which tracks are AI-generated. Spotify is labeling which musicians are AI and which are human. Apple is flagging AI-generated music so listeners can spot it.

  • Western Digital (WDC -0.55%) closed that day 65% under the record it reached on June 18, and Seagate Technology (STX -2.10%) finished 58% below its June 22 peak.
  • Put another way, investors look to be pricing in the end of this memory and storage boom.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Daniel Sparks – Nov 26, 2026 at 4:41AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Sandisk ›.

It has been revealed that sandisk (SNDK -5.57%) expects revenue of $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion this quarter, up from $11.0 billion last quarter. But as of the Nov. 20 close, the stock stood around 73% below its split-adjusted record close from June 25.

Sandisk isn't alone. Western Digital (WDC -0.55%) closed that day 65% under the record it reached on June 18, and Seagate Technology (STX -2.10%) finished 58% below its June 22 peak. SK Hynix (SKHY -0.75%) ended the day 48% below its Sept. 9 closing high, its lowest close since its July debut on the Nasdaq. All four rebounded sharply on Nov. 23, but each was still more than 30% below its peak.

Put another way, investors look to be pricing in the end of this memory and storage boom. But I think the sell-off has gone too far, given what these four companies are reporting.

Industry observers note that showing how much cash the flash memory maker now pulls in, Sandisk produced $6.3 billion of free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capital spending) in the three months through Oct. 2, its fiscal first quarter of 2027. That compares to $438 million a year before.

It has been revealed that even after $5.0 billion of buybacks, Sandisk closed the quarter with $5.1 billion of cash. It has no debt. And that one quarter of free cash flow is around 6% of the organization's market value of about $105 billion.

According to recent reports, growth is slowing, of course, from 23% sequentially in fiscal Q1 to about 12% at the midpoint of this quarter's guidance. But the midpoint of management's non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings guidance comes to around $7 per share after the 8-for-1 stock split. Multiply that by four, and the stock trades for only about 3 times earnings. That price arguably assumes most of today's profits vanish within a few years.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

Earlier this month, I estimated Western Digital stock could be worth around $500 by 2030 -- returns of about 8% a year from the $366 or so it traded at then. At about $300 as I write, the same $500 would mean returns of about 13% yearly, not counting dividends.

According to recent reports, the hard drive maker's adjusted earnings per share rose from $1.78 a year before to $3.56 in fiscal Q4 2026 and $4.64 in fiscal Q1 2027. Not only does management expect $5.80 in fiscal Q2 at the midpoint of its guidance, but it also expects revenue growth of 66% to 72% year over year, a rise from the 55% it just posted. That puts the stock at around 13 times annualized guided earnings.

Sources indicate that my estimate hasn't moved, but the price has. At this level, I think Western Digital shares are a buy.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

Seagate has used its jump in profits to pay down debt quickly. Its gross debt was around $3.6 billion on July 3. After retiring around $1.2 billion in its fiscal first quarter of 2027 and another $750 million after the quarter closed, it's down to $1.6 billion. Seagate had $1.3 billion in cash on Oct. 2, before the latest repayment.

In a recent development, also, Seagate's adjusted earnings per share almost tripled year over year to $7.68 in fiscal Q1. Management expects $9.20 in fiscal Q2.

At around $520, shares trade at about 14 times annualized guided earnings. That looks modest to me.

SK Hynix's third-quarter revenue grew 32% from the second quarter and 328% year over year, to around 104.6 trillion won. Operating profit soared 632% year over year to around 83.3 trillion won, an operating margin of about 80%.

Better yet, the South Korean chipmaker finished the quarter with 114.5 trillion won in cash and cash equivalents versus 15.8 trillion won in borrowings, for net cash of 98.7 trillion won. It also intends around 100 trillion won of shareholder returns for 2026.

Still, on expected 2027 earnings, SK Hynix's price-to-earnings ratio is only about 3. At that price, the market arguably expects profits to drop steeply long before 2030.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

Over a decade, I'd expect at least one memory bust. Flash memory, DRAM, and hard drive prices can all drop sharply when supply catches up, and these stocks could fall more before they recover.

But each company is using the boom to stockpile cash, cut debt, or buy back shares.

I'd buy all four today. Given how sharply these stocks can swing, I wouldn't let any of them become a major share of my portfolio. And I'd plan to hold through the next downturn rather than try to time it. Of course, that downturn could come earlier than I think.

#132137. Claude can ship code for you now – how to try it (if you dare)

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (891 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Zdnet ↗ Open Full Page

Claude can ship code for you now – how to try it (if you dare)

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (891 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it.
  • According to recent reports, with Claude Ship, revealed in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic stated.
  • Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it. A new feature from Anthropic is banking on more adventurous, agent-first coders being comfortable with handing even that last step off to AI.

According to recent reports, with Claude Ship, revealed in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic stated. The feature is geared toward individual developers or companies who want to move faster or already delegate a significant amount of coding tasks to agents.

Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code.

“Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person,” Anthropic stated. “The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.”.

The new feature uses two new agents alongside Code Review, which Anthropic released in March for Teams and Enterprise intends. Code Review first collects, organizes, and posts findings to a PR. Then, Anthropic said, the agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, guide a PR “through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don’t have to manage each step manually.”.

PR Steward can’t approve or merge pull requests, designed instead to participate “on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members.” It also documents what it changed in each push through comments and provides instructions for how to undo it, should developers want to. Throughout the process, developers can give Claude instructions or tell it to stop by commenting @claude.

Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free – how it went.

As a final step, Claude Approvals references whatever policy the user or team abides by (which developers provide as a repo file), and additional signals developers set, like Code Review findings, before approving changes autonomously if allowed. If not, it will seek out “deeper human sign-off,” Anthropic said.

“It works like a smarter CODEOWNERS file,” the release added. Anthropic remarked it recommends that most customers enable those additional checks “first in observe-only mode to build confidence before configuring branch protection to require Claude Approvals’ green light.”.

Admins can select which repos the feature runs in and adjust settings as needed.

But Claude Ship isn’t meant for everyone.

It has been revealed that “Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” Anthropic stated in the release, noting that its own Claude Code team uses Claude to write a majority of the code it needs.

ZDNET senior contributing editor David Gewirtz remarked the idea of shipping code at the speed of writing it “raises the hair on the back of my neck.” But he added that, given how impressive Claude Code has been thus far, he wouldn’t be surprised if Anthropic’s deployment tools were equally effective.

Industry observers note that also: Claude Code vs. Codex: Why I use both and how to choose one (if you must).

Industry observers note that “But, it does depend on the team’s workflow and the kind of development they’re doing,” he said. “It’s not something for every team and certainly not for every indy developer, but for certain deployment processes, it could shave a ton of time off turnaround, saving money and potentially sending fixes to customers much faster. ‘Tis cool.”.

Ultimately, Gewirtz said he has reasons to both trust the tool and be concerned about what it means for younger developers in the workplace.

“Since that workflow is often assigned to less experienced members of the team, it’s likely that Claude would be as accurate, although it’s one more way to shut the junior members out of where they add value to the manufacturer and grow their skills to become senior decision makers,” he mentioned.

Developer platforms overall are adapting to the new state of the industry. Entire, a GitHub competitor started by the Microsoft-owned platform’s former CEO, is built around the expectation that developers are working side-by-side with agents.

Individuals with a Pro, Max, or Ultra subscription can use the /ship command now available in Claude Code, meaning “users won’t notice any significant increase in token usage,” an Anthropic representative explained. Team and Enterprise users can use Claude Ship for Github repos, and it is billed on tokens, so your overall bill may change.

It has been revealed that still, that depends on the number of PRs users are putting through Claude Ship — to avoid any surprises, admins can set spending limits for both Code Review and the new PR Steward agent. They can also turn Claude Ship on for an entire repo, meaning developers won’t need the /ship command.

Anthropic added that certain Enterprise organizations “can claim at least $10,000 in Claude Ship credits to use within 30 days of claiming” by Jan. 15, 2027.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac – with Claude Code standing guard.

As with other Claude features, like the still-to-come Meetings, customers with a zero-data-retention policy and other privacy configurations don’t have access to Claude Ship.

#132132. Breaking: I Tried Using Meta Muse and ChatGPT Dots to Save on Groceries. They’re Not Quite There Yet

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1184 w)
📖 Baca

Breaking: I Tried Using Meta Muse and ChatGPT Dots to Save on Groceries. They’re Not Quite There Yet

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1184 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, high grocery prices have been in the news for years now.
  • So before you drop a fortune on gas and drive out to the grocery store to spend even more on sustenance in your prep for hosting or bringing dishes to your holiday celebrations, you might consider using an AI agent to find you the best deal possible.
  • Recent findings suggest that although, in my experience, it’s not as simple as the AI marketing makes it sound.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, high grocery prices have been in the news for years now. The cost of eggs, how much you’re paying for a bowl of cereal and whether or not meat is back on the menu are the recurring subjects of nationwide headlines.

So before you drop a fortune on gas and drive out to the grocery store to spend even more on sustenance in your prep for hosting or bringing dishes to your holiday celebrations, you might consider using an AI agent to find you the best deal possible.

Recent findings suggest that although, in my experience, it’s not as simple as the AI marketing makes it sound. Here’s what happened when I tried to use AI agents to find the lowest possible prices on groceries.

AI agents such as Meta Muse and ChatGPT’s Dots can only crawl so many sites and online fliers for prices. Some stores and e-commerce sites have blocked AI agents from accessing their URLs. The first step in finding cheaper groceries with AI agents is to check which sites and stores they can access for price comparisons.

Where both agents missed a step was in the limitations they put on their searches, at first only looking at the retailers I had shown via my receipts and a few other massive-name grocery stores.

I clarified in the chats and in a 20-minute voice conversation with Muse and a 14-minute voice conversation with Dots that they should expand their horizons and look at discount online retailers like Martie.com, and check what they could around advertised pricing and offerings at local farmers’ markets.

Muse stuck to the basics like Ralphs, Target and Walmart, and then expanded to Sprouts, Vons and Martie.com when prompted.

After further nudging, Muse also reviewed user-reported pricing from Costco (I don’t have a membership), gave me vague information about Grocery Outlet, suggested Misfits Market/Imperfect Foods, ruled out Amazon Fresh and gave me some sample pricing from a local butcher for meats.

Muse also checked some local bakery prices after I mentioned I’d like to find alternatives to sweet treats at a more affordable price.

Dots checked all the usual places that Meta Muse checked with a few extras thrown in — Smart & Final for produce, meat and some packaged products, and Super King’s monthly ad.

It has been revealed that neither of the tools checked Trader Joe’s. Muse said that the grocery chain doesn’t show prices of its products online, despite me finding that the Trader Joe’s website indicates prices of its products online. Both Dots and Muse admitted to only checking the local store’s pages when asked.

You could spend some time making a list from scratch of all the groceries you might need every two weeks and give that list to the AI agent for its search. You could also skip all that and take some pics of your most recent grocery receipts and online payments and have the AI agent build the list itself.

According to recent reports, I had some receipts saved, and the AI agents I used for this test were able to put together an accurate grocery list from them. I also provided emails showing receipts from online orders of household items and groceries for the past month to build my orders.

Industry observers note that muse took my receipts and concluded that, surprise, surprise, shopping at Gelson’s was not as cost-effective as shopping at Walmart. It spat out a lot of specific information about comparisons on some of the items in my list, but completely ignored others.

Dots looked over my receipts and recommended I try shopping at Super King for most fresh meat, produce and a few grains, and keep Walmart as my main option for packaged products like pasta sauce.

Both tools tackled this task in a way I was not expecting — as a narrative exploration of my overall grocery spending, with generalized suggestions supported by specific examples of spot pricing.

It was kind of like they’ve been optimized to write essays about grocery shopping as a school assignment, and not to be agentic personal assistants for real-world work.

Maybe it was the way I phrased the task, but I was hoping to get an actual shopping list with price comparisons for each item, or at least equivalent items, and a guide on where and how to procure said items.

Neither AI agent provided this autonomously and had to be directly prompted to provide grocery lists in response to a very specific request.

AI agents are supposed to be pros at anticipating the needs of their human bosses. I was keen to see how the always-on AI agents would handle managing the recurring needs of a small household and if they might make any autonomous suggestions meant to save me money in ways I hadn’t anticipated.

Sources indicate that at no point did Muse seem to be actually thinking outside the strict parameters of the review of the items on the receipts I sent. This felt more like a conversation about what I’d previously purchased with a side serving of attempts to get me to connect Instacart to the tool.

It was also the most confusing grocery shopping experience I have ever had. That might be on me, but I would assume the agent might ask some questions, like how often I usually shop, what my monthly budget for groceries is, and how many people and animals live in the house. Muse didn’t ask any of those things and had to be prompted consistently.

According to recent reports, muse sent me the final grocery list as a raw Markdown file, which was hilarious. I got a .pdf version after explicitly asking for one.

Industry observers note that my original total with one in-person shop and one online order was about $180. Muse’s total with three in-person shops and one online order came in at around $153.

Dots was slightly better suited to this task after some prodding, and gave me some options for building prep meals with low-effort, high-protein recipes based on how I usually shop.

Dots’ final grocery list included everything I asked for, but still missed some key items, like solid substitutes for pricey prepped foods. Dot’s final total with two in-person shopping trips and a whole lot of missing items came out to around $85.

This test reinforced my findings about how agentic AI tools tackle domestic or traditionally invisible labor tasks. In my limited use cases so far, they are about as useful as a loose dog turd tumbling around in a clothes dryer.

If you’re not looking to book a flight and hotel for a business conference in Philadelphia or put your Sweetgreen order on autopilot, the AI agents exhibit a startling lack of curiosity and autonomous thinking.

Recent findings suggest that there’s still a large gap in common sense on the part of agentic AI for those of us hoping these tools will make our everyday lives outside of a 9-to-5 easier, more affordable or less hectic. I hope that changes as they learn.

#132128. How to Prepare for RMDs Starting at 75 — Even If You're Only 60 Right Now

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (661 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

How to Prepare for RMDs Starting at 75 — Even If You're Only 60 Right Now

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (661 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that fifteen years might seem like a long way in the future.
  • Required Minimum Distributions (RMDs) may feel like a problem to deal with later if you're 60 years old.
  • Here are four specific actions a 60-year-old can take right now to meaningfully reduce the RMD burden at 75.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Keith Speights – Nov 26, 2026 at 4:44AM EST.

It has been revealed that fifteen years might seem like a long way in the future. However, time goes by promptly.

Required Minimum Distributions (RMDs) may feel like a problem to deal with later if you're 60 years old. After all, for anyone born in 1960 or later, the tax obligation doesn't start until age 75. But that instinct is precisely what makes RMDs the most expensive retirement-planning mistake people make. The decisions available at 60 are worth far more than any RMD strategy available at 74 -- and by the time most people start thinking about this, the best options have already closed.

Here are four specific actions a 60-year-old can take right now to meaningfully reduce the RMD burden at 75.

1. Run the projection now, not at 74.

Industry observers note that the first step is understanding what your RMD will actually be. The IRS calculates RMDs by dividing the prior year-end account balance by a life expectancy factor from the Uniform Lifetime Table -- approximately 24.6 for a 75-year-old. A 60-year-old with $500,000 in a traditional IRA today, growing at 7% annually, will have around $1.29 million by the end of the year they turn 74, implying a first-year RMD of roughly $52,400. Running that projection now creates the awareness that motivates everything else on this list.

Sources indicate that 2. Begin Roth conversions in the low-tax window.

The years between 60 and 74 -- particularly before Social Security begins and before RMDs start -- are typically the lowest-tax period of a retiree's financial life. Converting traditional IRA funds to Roth IRAs during this window pays today's tax rate on the converted amount in exchange for permanently removing that balance from future RMD calculations. Even modest annual conversions of $20,000 to $50,000 over 15 years can meaningfully shrink the RMD burden at 75. Importantly, Roth IRAs have no RMDs at all during the original owner's lifetime.

Industry observers note that 3. Coordinate conversions with claiming Social Security.

In a recent development, the interaction between Roth conversions and Social Security taxation is the most underappreciated element of pre-RMD planning. Converting aggressively before Social Security begins keeps provisional income below the thresholds that trigger taxation on up to 85% of benefits. This can save thousands of dollars annually throughout retirement. The window for this strategy is finite and closes the moment both Social Security and RMDs begin arriving simultaneously.

4. Consider a qualified longevity annuity contract.

The SECURE 2.0 Act allows retirees to use up to $210,000 (in 2026) of IRA funds to purchase a qualified longevity annuity contract (QLAC) -- a deferred income annuity that begins payments at a future date, typically 80 or 85. The limit is adjusted for inflation over time. Funds used for a QLAC are excluded from RMD calculations until the annuity begins paying, effectively reducing the RMD base and deferring both the income and the tax.

Age 60 isn't too soon to prepare.

The most expensive RMD is the one that arrives as a surprise at 75 from an IRA that was never touched between 60 and 74. The least expensive one is the result of 15 years of quiet, deliberate preparation -- Roth conversions in low-tax years, careful Social Security coordination, and a QLAC that removes a portion of the IRA balance from the RMD calculation entirely.

The problem doesn't feel urgent at 60. That's exactly why starting now produces such dramatically better outcomes than waiting until it does.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Google has added Wallet integration to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode, letting you learn about your spending habits, plan a budget, maximize credit card rewards, and more with a simple Search.
    • Starting today, Google confirmed, Personal Intelligence for Search is expanding to more apps, including Wallet and Drive.
    • Also: I tried Personal Intelligence in Android Auto – and it knew exactly where I wanted to go.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Google has added Wallet integration to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode, letting you learn about your spending habits, plan a budget, maximize credit card rewards, and more with a simple Search.

    Starting today, Google confirmed, Personal Intelligence for Search is expanding to more apps, including Wallet and Drive. Google can’t move or manage any money, but it can give you tailored, personalized search results about your finances, like showing where you spend the most, identifying recurring subscriptions you might not be aware of, and suggesting which credit card might be best to use for travel. All you have to do is ask in a search.

    Also: I tried Personal Intelligence in Android Auto – and it knew exactly where I wanted to go.

    This feature comes just over a week after Google introduced Personal Intelligence to Wallet.

    According to recent reports, once your Wallet is connected, it takes a few minutes to fully sync. Once it’s finished, you can ask questions through AI mode in Search.

    I decided to give it a try for myself, starting off with a simple query: “Based on my spending, what’s a quick way I can save money?” I could have told you one of the primary culprits, but Google happily responded with what I already knew: far too much of my money goes to fast food and coffee.

    “You frequently grab quick-service meals,” the response mentioned, pointing out several fast food places that I do indeed frequent, “and specialty coffees throughout the week.” If I just cut that down to two meals and two coffees a week, Gemini explained, I’d save about $30 a week, or $1,500 a year.

    Also: This powerful Gemini setting made my AI results way more personal and accurate.

    It has been revealed that when I asked it to find recurring subscriptions, Gemini noted that I had several monthly charges. What I didn’t ask for, but it did, was to break down those subscriptions into an easy-to-see chart, complete with the name, price, category, the card it’s being charged to, and the timeframe it usually comes out. Gemini even offered a few free alternatives to services I was paying for.

    Sources indicate that since Gemini also knows what cards are linked to your Wallet, it’s able to offer advice there, too. I’m planning a trip to Upcoming York City, so I asked which cards might be best to use for the hotels and airfare. Gemini was able to analyze my card benefits, considering things like rewards and built-in travel insurance, and make a recommendation.

    According to recent reports, also: Slow Android phone? How to speed it back up in 4 easy steps.

    Recent findings suggest that while Gemini Personal Intelligence can access your Gmail to learn more about your spending, it can’t access your bank account. The only information it knows about your finances and spending comes from receipts in your inbox or from your Wallet transaction history. I do use Wallet often (mostly when ordering through online apps), but it’s not quite my go-to option when I’m in a store. Given how useful this feature can be, though, I might just start using Wallet more to give it more information to work with.

Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.

    Industry observers note that "Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," mentioned the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Can Shiba Inu Reach $1 in 2027? The Answer Might Shock You.

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (834 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that the Shiba Inu (SHIB +5.74%) cryptocurrency was created in 2020 by an anonymous developer named Ryoshi, who saw the success of Dogecoin and wanted to build a more useful alternative.
    • In a recent development, shiba Inu soared by a whopping 45,278,000% in 2021, a return so strong that it could have turned a perfectly-timed investment of $3 into over $1 million.
    • However, speculation was the primary driver of the 2021 rally, so it simply wasn't sustainable.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Anthony Di Pizio – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:07AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Shiba Inu ›.

    Sources indicate that the Shiba Inu (SHIB +5.74%) cryptocurrency was created in 2020 by an anonymous developer named Ryoshi, who saw the success of Dogecoin and wanted to build a more useful alternative. Shiba Inu runs on the Ethereum (ETH +2.68%) network, so it inherits all of the functionality, security, and infrastructure of the world's biggest platform for developing decentralized software applications.

    In a recent development, shiba Inu soared by a whopping 45,278,000% in 2021, a return so strong that it could have turned a perfectly-timed investment of $3 into over $1 million. It's one of the largest single-year gains in the history of the financial markets, so it's no surprise many investors still watch this token.

    However, speculation was the primary driver of the 2021 rally, so it simply wasn't sustainable. Shiba Inu has since lost 96% of its peak value, and trades at just $0.0000036 per token as I write this on Nov. 24. But there is one way Shiba Inu could stage another historic bull run, and potentially even reach $1 per token. Can it happen in 2027? The answer might shock you.

    Having a legitimate source of demand is the key to sustainable upside for any asset. People buy real estate because houses have utility, and they buy stocks because the underlying companies generate revenue and earnings. Many cryptocurrencies also have real use-cases that attract demand, although whether it will last over the long term is up for debate.

    XRP (XRP +4.84%), for example, is the native cryptocurrency in Ripple's payment network. It helps banks send money around the world instantly, and with minimal fees. Then there is Ether, the native coin in the Ethereum network, which is used to pay fees that cover the computing costs when people use decentralized software applications.

    Since Shiba Inu is built on Ethereum, customers can program smart contracts to establish autonomous rules when using the token on decentralized platforms like lending marketplaces and crypto exchanges. Developers created a Layer-2 blockchain solution called Shibarium to improve transaction speeds and reduce costs, but it hasn't necessarily made the Shiba Inu ecosystem any more popular.

    It has been revealed that unlike Ether, Shiba Inu isn't required to build decentralized apps or cover the associated fees. Plus, while it can technically be used as a payment mechanism, just 1,254 businesses around the world are willing to accept it in exchange for goods and services (according to Cryptwerk).

    According to recent reports, in short, Shiba Inu continues to lack a true use case, and the subsequent lack of organic demand is the main reason it has lost 96% of its peak value. However, there's an even bigger issue standing in the way of a meaningful recovery.

    CRYPTO · As of 11:00 AM ET 11/26/26.

    Shiba Inu has a circulating supply of 589.2 trillion tokens, so at the current price of $0.0000036 per token, it has a market capitalization of $2.15 billion. Therefore, basic math suggests that a price of $1 per token would result in a market cap of $589.2 trillion, which would make Shiba Inu almost nine times as valuable as all 500 companies in the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.25%) combined.

    Such a high valuation is impossible to justify, so there is no way Shiba Inu will reach $1 as things presently stand. However, the community is trying to resolve the supply problem by "burning" tokens, which typically involves sending them to a dead wallet where they can never be retrieved. In theory, the price per token should increase in proportion to the number of tokens taken out of circulation, creating a real potential pathway to the $1 milestone.

    Based on Shiba Inu's market cap of $2.15 billion, burning 99.99998% of the 589.2 trillion tokens currently in supply could result in a price of $1 per token.

    According to recent reports, however, only 349 million tokens were burned in October, which equates to an annualized rate of 4.2 billion. It would take an eye-popping 140,285 years to burn enough supply to justify a price of $1 per token at this pace, so it definitely won't happen in 2027.

    But there is even more bad news. Burning tokens doesn't create any real value, so nobody will make any money. Every investor would simply have 99.99998% fewer tokens, so even though each token would be worth $1, their net financial position won't have changed.

    Well, actually, 140,000 years' worth of inflation would make the descendents of each investor significantly worse off.

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (419 w)

    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Zdnet ↗ Open Full Page

    Gen Z is the least interested in AI at work – and it’s not even close

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (419 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Zdnet

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that generation Z might have the lowest morale around AI at work compared to other generations.
    • Gen Z, which includes those born between 1997 and 2012, expressed the least interest and found the least utility in AI, Seramount found.
    • Also: OpenAI is offering small businesses free AI support – and up to $8K/mo to experts who help them.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that generation Z might have the lowest morale around AI at work compared to other generations. That’s according to a survey from talent services firm Seramount, which found that Gen Z was the most AI-averse among the generations surveyed about using the technology in their jobs.

    Gen Z, which includes those born between 1997 and 2012, expressed the least interest and found the least utility in AI, Seramount found. Only 18% of Gen Z reported an interest in strengthening their AI skills, compared to 36% of Millennials, 46% of Gen Xers, and 43% of Boomers. Gen Z is also using AI less than other generations, by nine percentage points.

    Also: OpenAI is offering small businesses free AI support – and up to $8K/mo to experts who help them.

    “Employers cannot assume their youngest employees will embrace AI on their own,” said Diana Forster, senior director of research at Seramount.

    The survey polled responses from over 1,800 US white-collar workers at companies with at least 500 employees.

    In a recent development, around half of Gen Z report weekly AI use (not specific to work), according to a survey from Walton Family Foundation, GSV Ventures and Gallup, but the generation’s skepticism has mounted over the past few years. Even members of Gen Z who use AI daily have less positive views on the technology. In the same study, 42% of Gen Z reported feeling anxious about AI in 2026, a 1% increase from 2025. Last year, 36% of Gen Z respondents reported excitement about AI. In 2026, that percentage dropped to 22%.

    Also: These companies are actually upskilling their workers for AI – here’s how they do it.

    It’s no surprise Gen Z is skeptical about adopting a technology that could be undermining their own career development. The labor market has been particularly harsh to this group of workers, as entry-level job postings have fallen in recent years, and many fear that AI will only exacerbate unemployment. Around 8% of those ages 22 to 24 were unemployed in September, compared to 3% of workers ages 25 to 54, according to data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

    But with many workplaces still adopting AI, senior employees are trying to prepare Gen Z by getting them on board at work.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that anthropic is making its Claude artifacts available as desktop apps, meaning you can share and more easily access your most-repeated tasks on your computer.
    • Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.
    • Anthropic first released artifacts in 2024.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that anthropic is making its Claude artifacts available as desktop apps, meaning you can share and more easily access your most-repeated tasks on your computer. The “install as app” feature is available in beta for all free and paid Claude plans and works on both Mac and Windows, but not Linux.

    Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.

    Anthropic first released artifacts in 2024. Since then, they’ve become a way to standardize and repeat tasks users do regularly, especially at work. Previously, artifacts ran via your Claude window or in a browser. By splicing them out as distinct desktop apps, you can now run different Claude queries while also using your artifacts locally, or use those apps without opening Claude at all.

    “When an artifact is installed as a Mac or Windows app, it gets its own icon and opens in its own window instead of inside Claude. You can share it with others, and it needs your permission before it can interact with your computer,” Anthropic said.

    Sources indicate that artifact apps can still access Claude and any connectors you’re using, and they patch automatically when you edit the artifact itself in Claude. When apps request something from Claude, though, that goes toward your Claude usage limits, which are lowest for free people.

    Anthropic mentioned the app feature is meant to streamline building apps for both developer and non-developer work.

    In a recent development, also: Can AI plan terrorist attacks? US tested ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok.

    The revision clarifies where AI software for work is headed. Claude is already more of an AI-powered work suite than a single helpful chatbot for many organizations. Evidently, people are using tools like artifacts frequently enough — and simultaneously with other Claude features — that they need those Claude-based tools to function like discrete bits of software on their own.

    “If you rely on a tool for work, it should open like the rest of your apps and remind you when something needs your attention,” Anthropic mentioned.

    Recent findings suggest that claude artifact apps don’t have the same functionality as apps you could build using Claude Code, though. Even if you don’t need Claude open for these apps to work, you’ll still need to be signed in to Claude and have internet access, so they’re not an entirely portable or off-grid option.

    The feature’s support page also notes that legacy artifacts, “live artifacts from Claude Cowork,” and artifacts generated from templates like Docs, Slides, and Sheets can’t be installed as desktop apps.

    According to recent reports, first, make sure Claude for Mac or Windows is updated. You can try the “install as app” feature, which is in beta for all free and paid aims, via Claude’s Share menu. Select the Install as app option, which will then download the artifact you chose to your desktop. From there, set permissions as needed.

    Permissions range from the default (whatever they are in a browser) to app-specific permissions like sending notifications and full computer access.

    Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free.

    Sources indicate that full computer access means the artifact app can “run programs and read, change, or delete your files without asking each time,” Anthropic stated, so proceed carefully. Every time you edit and revision the artifact (and thus the app), Claude will ask you to confirm permissions again, so you’ll ideally have regular checkpoints to revise access. Still, there are some guardrails in place: Anthropic only lets you give full computer access to apps you’ve made yourself. For Team and Enterprise plans, that extends to any apps made by your coworkers.

    “Anthropic doesn’t review apps before you install them, so only give full access to apps you trust,” the organization stated.

    For Claude Enterprise aims, the install-as-app feature is off entirely until an admin turns it on in Organization settings.
