    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Trevor Jennewine – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:12AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    Recent findings suggest that the U.S. stock market has come under considerable pressure in recent weeks. The benchmark S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.25%) and the technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -0.62%) have dropped into correction territory, falling approximately 10% and 17%, respectively, from their October highs.

    Corporate earnings growth has been exceptional this year, but investors are increasingly worried that technology companies are spending too much money on artificial intelligence infrastructure. Persistent inflation and the expectation of higher interest rates have also contributed to the sell-off.

    Recent findings suggest that unfortunately, President Donald Trump just gave investors another reason to worry, and the news comes at a particularly bad time. On Nov. 25, his administration proposed fresh tariffs targeting 14 major trading partners, including China and the European Union. Those import taxes threaten to complicate the Federal Reserve's fight against inflation, which could hurt the stock market.

    Sources indicate that image source: Official White House Photo by Joyce N. Boghosian.

    In May, President Trump said, "My favorite word in the dictionary is tariff." He believes tariffs could be a substantial source of revenue for the federal government, while also bolstering national security by incentivizing companies to move manufacturing operations to the United States.

    However, several studies suggest tariffs imposed by the Trump administration have already increased costs for American businesses, and those businesses often pass at least a portion of the additional expense along to consumers in the form of higher prices.

    Additionally, economists at the Newly introduced York Fed identified another troubling phenomenon in a recent research paper: Tariffs have actually increased the price of domestically produced goods, partly because American manufacturers use imported materials and partly because they face less competition from foreign businesses.

    Those indirect price increases took as long as 12 months to work their way through supply chains, meaning inflationary consequences of higher tariffs are not necessarily apparent immediately. Regardless, history makes it clear that the latest round of import taxes could drive inflation higher.

    The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter percentage point in September due to persistent inflation, bringing the target range on the federal funds rate to 3.75% to 4%. Fed officials held rates steady at the October meeting, but CME Group's FedWatch tool highlights another rate hike is widely anticipated in December.

    President Trump's latest tariff proposals could keep inflation elevated for longer, forcing the Federal Reserve to maintain tighter monetary policy or raise interest rates even further. Indeed, EY chief economist Greg Daco warned that newly introduced tariffs increase the risk of a "more hawkish Fed response." And that could spell trouble for the stock market.

    Recent findings suggest that higher interest rates tend to suppress consumer and business spending, creating a headwind to corporate earnings growth. They also make bonds more attractive relative to stocks, putting downward pressure on equity valuations.

    Sources indicate that nevertheless, investors have reason for optimism. Despite Trump's latest tariffs, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanely believe the S&P 500 will reach 8,700 next year; that implies 21% upside from its current level of 7,182. UBS is even more optimistic, with a year-end target of 8,900, implying 24% upside. As always, investors should remain calm through market turbulence, and treat significant dips as buying opportunities.

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (601 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s request to launch 1 million AI-equipped satellites to create vast data centers in space.
    • SpaceX initially filed an application in May asking for permission to launch the satellites, collectively known as Starmind.
    • “It’s just really abrogating their responsibility to go, ‘Well, this is a project they’re proposing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s request to launch 1 million AI-equipped satellites to create vast data centers in space.

    SpaceX initially filed an application in May asking for permission to launch the satellites, collectively known as Starmind. The FCC’s approval requires that SpaceX launch its first data center satellite by 2030 and meet the 1 million mark by 2040.

    “It’s just really abrogating their responsibility to go, ‘Well, this is a project they’re proposing. Is this actually safe?’” Jonathan McDowell, an astrophysicist who tracks satellite debuts, told CNET. “It’s a blank check. Launch as many satellites as you can, and we’ll just see what happens. I think this is a mistake on the FCC’s part.”.

    Orbital data centers have long been a goal of SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, becoming a pivotal part of his pitch to investors ahead of the organization’s IPO in June.

    Sources indicate that “You’re power-constrained on Earth. Space has the advantage that it’s always sunny,” Musk mentioned in March.

    According to recent reports, on its web page for Starmind, SpaceX touts its high-efficiency solar arrays on the planned satellites and the cooling benefits of space. It states that high-speed laser links will beam the AI results back to Earth through Starlink’s constellation.

    In a recent development, space experts I’ve talked to this year about Starmind have been skeptical. The technical challenges alone are dizzying; the scale of SpaceX’s ambitions is hard to swallow.

    It’s taken seven years for Starlink to grow its constellation to 11,195 satellites, and that was already an unprecedented feat. Is it possible to get to 1 million satellites in 14 years?

    In a recent development, “We do not have the launch capacity for any of this,” Ian Christensen, senior director at the Secure World Foundation, told me in a previous interview. “Not even within SpaceX to do their own constellation, let alone the other constellations planned.”.

    According to recent reports, spaceX has increasingly prioritized launching its own satellites instead of letting commercial customers hitch a ride on their rockets. Starlink’s share of SpaceX missions has gone from 54% of its Falcon 9 rocket’s missions in 2020 to about 79% in 2026, according to a Reuters analysis. One analysis estimates that SpaceX would have to launch 5,000 Starship rockets a year to meet its goal — a staggering increase from 330 rockets that launched last year in total.

    Scientists have already been ringing alarm bells about overcrowded orbits as they exist now. The more satellites in space, the more difficult it is for operators to maneuver around each other. A single crash could turn into decades of orbital debris, which could cause a chain reaction that eventually makes space inoperable for everyone. And burning up all those satellites in the atmosphere when they reach the end of their lives has already started to leave ozone-depleting aluminum particles behind. A paper published this week in Earth and Space Chemistry estimated that SpaceX’s data center plan would multiply pollutants in the upper atmosphere by more than 150 times compared to last year.

    “There are scientific papers out there raising challenges,” McDowell said. “Yes, they’re unproven, but if I say, ‘Yeah, we’re not sure if this is going to destroy the atmosphere and kill us all, but it might,’ is the right reaction to go, ‘Well, you haven’t proven it, so we’re just going to ignore it’?”.

    The FCC’s approval came despite objections from Amazon, the environmental nonprofit Public Employees for Environmental Responsibility and the American Astronomical Society.

    A representative for SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

    Breaking: Etihad’s New Credit Cards Are Primarily for Status Chasers

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1289 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that etihad Guest, the loyalty program of Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, is expanding its U.S.
    • The two cards are the Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card ($99 annual fee) and the Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card ($499 annual fee).
    • Industry observers note that they also offer extra miles on international transactions (neither has foreign transaction fees) and purchases with Etihad’s partner airlines, which include U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that etihad Guest, the loyalty program of Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, is expanding its U.S. presence by introducing two new credit cards. Most people won’t get much value from these cards, but they can make sense for Etihad frequent flyers who want elite status.

    The two cards are the Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card ($99 annual fee) and the Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card ($499 annual fee). Issued by the First National Bank of Omaha, both offer faster pathways to earning and maintaining elite status and the ability to earn extra miles on Etihad purchases.

    Industry observers note that they also offer extra miles on international transactions (neither has foreign transaction fees) and purchases with Etihad’s partner airlines, which include U.S. carriers like American Airlines and JetBlue Airways.

    Here’s what you need to know about the cards.

    The Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card comes with a $99 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

    3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

    2 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

    It has been revealed that 2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

    1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

    Welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the card is offering the following welcome offer for upcoming applicants: Earn up to 40,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 10,000 miles after the first purchase and an additional 30,000 miles after spending $3,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

    Sources indicate that elite status benefits: You’ll also get Etihad Silver status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account. Unlike most airlines, that entry-level status is enough to get you into the business class lounge when traveling through Etihad’s hub at Abu Dhabi’s Zayed International Airport.

    You can retain that status by spending $20,000 a year on the card, or $3,000 a year on Etihad purchases.

    The Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card comes with a $499 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

    5 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

    3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

    2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

    In a recent development, 1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

    The only differences in rewards between the premium and standard cards are increased earning rates for eligible airline purchases.

    Welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the premium card offers a higher welcome offer compared to the standard card: Earn up to 60,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 20,000 miles after the first purchase and 40,000 miles after spending $7,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

    Elite status benefits: The premium card offers a faster track to elite status: automatic Silver status upon card approval and Gold status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account.

    To maintain Gold status, you’ll need to spend $40,000 a year on the card, or $8,000 on Etihad purchases. Otherwise, you’ll have Silver status.

    In a recent development, wi-Fi benefit: After your first Etihad purchase, you’ll get 3,000 Etihad Guest miles, enough to cover Wi-Fi costs on a long-haul Etihad flight. You’ll then get those miles again after each cardholder anniversary.

    It has been revealed that travel benefits: The card offers a statement credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck and select travel protections. If you already have a premium travel card, you might already have access to these perks.

    According to recent reports, the card also includes a Priority Pass lounge access membership. However, an Etihad spokesperson told NerdWallet that it’s the entry-level membership tier, so you’ll need to pay for yourself and guests each time you visit a Priority Pass lounge. Most premium credit cards in the U.S. that offer Priority Pass allow complimentary visits for at least the cardholder.

    The Etihad cards make the most sense for Etihad’s frequent flyers who are flying to or connecting through Abu Dhabi several times a year.

    That’s because the standard card’s accelerated pathway to Etihad Guest’s Silver status tier can unlock the ability to choose business class lounge access in Abu Dhabi as a status perk.

    With the premium card, you get a fast track to Gold. If you select lounge access as a Gold status perk, you can not only bring a guest on the same flight into the lounge, but also access Etihad’s worldwide lounge network. That includes Etihad’s own lounges in Newly introduced York and Washington, D.C., as well as most partner lounges at other Etihad destinations.

    In a recent development, bear in mind that while Etihad has many partnerships with other airlines, it’s not part of an alliance, so you don’t get lounge benefits when traveling on partners. You’ll need to be flying on an Etihad-operated flight to get into the lounge.

    If you primarily fly with other carriers, then Etihad status will have limited upside for you.

    According to recent reports, however, the Priority Pass lounge membership that comes with the premium card does not have that restriction. You can access Priority Pass lounges while flying on any airline, although you’ll need to pay an additional per-person $35 fee each visit.

    According to recent reports, the earning rates on the Etihad cards are lackluster for everyday spenders. The bonus categories are for airline purchases with Etihad and its partners, as well as international spending.

    That means your day-to-day purchases at home, like groceries, dining out and gas, earn only 1 mile per $1 spent.

    Sources indicate that plus, there are more ways to earn Etihad Guest miles than spending on an Etihad credit card. For example, you can transfer points to Etihad Guest from Bilt Rewards, Capital One and Citi ThankYou.

    Recent findings suggest that those programs offer cards that typically have better benefits and bonus categories, and they offer flexibility on how you can use your points and miles. With an Etihad card, you can only earn Etihad Guest miles, which expire after 18 months without qualifying flight activity. (If you’re not traveling on Etihad or its partners at least once every 18 months, then you definitely should not get the cards.).

    Sources indicate that one of the most interesting perks of the new cards is the bonus category for spending with Etihad partner airlines — 2 miles per $1 for the standard card and 3 miles per $1 for the premium version. Typically, airline credit cards reward customers only for spending on the airline, not partners.

    There are better cards available, though. Some offer as many or even more points per $1 on flights purchased directly from airlines.

    If you want the card solely to earn more Etihad Guest miles, then the answer for most people is no.

    While you can earn more miles for purchases with Etihad and partner airlines, the earning rates aren’t attractive enough to justify the annual fees, especially when compared with existing cards with currencies that transfer to Etihad Guest.

    Status chasers could benefit from the fast track to elite status — but you would need to be a fairly frequent Etihad flyer to really take advantage of your elite benefits.

    It has been revealed that you want a travel credit card that prioritizes what’s important to you. Here are some of the best travel credit cards of 2026:.

    Flexibility, point transfers and a large bonus: Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card.

    No annual fee: Wells Fargo Autograph® Card.

    Flat-rate travel rewards: Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card.

    Bonus travel rewards and high-end perks: Chase Sapphire Reserve®.

    Luxury perks: American Express Platinum Card®.

    Business travelers: Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Choosing the best headphones of the year isn’t as cut-and-dry a process as other tech categories. All of our ears are different, so what sounds good is ultimately subjective. However, there are plenty of other benchmarks beyond sound quality and noise-canceling performance that make a pair of headphones stand out to us and receive our Editors’ Choice award.

    We’ve awarded headphones that debut with significant, tangible upgrades over their predecessors, such as the Sennheiser Momentum 5 and the Sonos Ace Ultra. Headphones with a unique and useful feature, like the Beats 360’s purpose-changing earpads, also catch our attention.

    Also: ZDNET’s best products of 2026: Expert picks for phones, laptops, and more.

    We also like headphones that embrace the latest wireless and audio technologies, such as LE Audio and Auracast, which is exactly what the Sony WF-1000XM6 does. I’ve had a chance to go hands-on with dozens of headphones this year, but these two stand out for their combination of features, audio quality, and value relative to price.

    The Beats 360 earned their spot as ZDNET’s pick for best headphones of the year, thanks to their unique take on earpad modularity, innovative audio engineering, sweat- and water-resistance, and native compatibility with Apple and Android. Beats created a pair of modular headphones that change functionality when you switch their earpads: the Performance Knit cushions are sweat-wicking and suited for exercise, while the UltraPlush cushions provide a comfortable, casual, and immersive listening experience.

    Since I got the Beats 360, I’ve retired my AirPods Pro 3 at the gym. Upgraded GymKit functionality in iOS 27 allows me to track cardio workouts from my iPhone, and I don’t have to worry about the 360 slipping off my head; I just don’t need my AirPods anymore. The Beats 360 include the Performance Knit cushions with purchase, and a pair of UltraPlush cushions is $50. That’ll bring your total to $400, but you’re getting two headphones in one.

    Sennheiser’s Momentum 5 debuted with significant upgrades over the Momentum 4, including a more detailed equalizer, a sleeker design, Dolby Atmos optimization, and improved ANC, making it more competitive with its contemporaries from Sony, Bose, and Apple. Sennheiser doesn’t beat any of its premium competitors in ANC, but it’s very close. Still, the Momentum 5 has something its competitors don’t: an easily self-repairable battery.

    Read our review: Sennheiser Momentum 5.

    It has been revealed that I love the Momentum 5’s detailed and balanced sound, hours-long comfort, and marathon battery life, which Sennheiser indicates delivers 57 hours of uninterrupted playtime. The Momentum 5 supports several hi-res AptX codecs and lossless audio via a wired USB-C connection. Regardless of whether your devices are Android, iOS, Windows, or anything else, you can access the Momentum 5’s full suite of features.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.
    • According to recent reports, here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept.
    • Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

    According to recent reports, here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

    Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

    Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

    Sources indicate that robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly notable sources of transaction revenue, while the tech giant has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

    According to recent reports, transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

    Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

    Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

    Net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

    —With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.
